(Prior Code, § 33.15) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.22 PHYSICAL ABILITY TEST.
   (A)   Each applicant shall be required to satisfactorily complete a physical
ability test at a place and time selected by the city. The purpose of the
evaluation is to determine, as accurately as possible, the ability of the
applicant to cope with the extreme physical stress of a firefighter. The same
evaluation shall be given to each applicant regardless of gender and evaluated
using accepted standards and norms for the position of firefighter. The
physical ability test shall be administered by Ashland Fire Department
personnel designated by the Fire Chief.
   (B)   All applicants will be assigned a time of arrival for the physical
ability test. Candidates shall enter the building no more than five minutes
prior to their assigned arrival time. Applicants will be instructed on where to
enter the building and where to park their vehicles in the hiring packet issued
to them prior to the test. Each applicant shall have a state or federal issued
ID and any other documentation requested in the hiring packet with them at the
time of arrival. Failure to present these items shall constitute automatic
removal from the process.
   (C)   The physical ability test shall be set up in an obstacle course
fashion. Each applicant shall receive an instruction packet prior to the
testing date explaining the testing procedures and grading criteria. The
applicant will be afforded the opportunity to ask any questions prior to the
start of the test. While completing the test, the applicant may ask the proctor
any questions, however, their time will continue and does not stop.
   (D)   To ensure the highest level of safety and to prevent applicants from
exhaustion, no running is allowed between events. A short walk between events
will be marked. This will permit the applicants to prepare for the next event.
Each event path shall be marked. Prior to starting the evaluation, applicants
will have vitals obtained (heart rate and blood pressure) and have them
rechecked after completing the evaluation.
   (E)   During the test, applicants must wear long pants. No open heel or open
toe shoes will be allowed. A 50 pound vest, to simulate the weight of the
firefighter protective equipment, gloves and hard hat will also be worn. In
addition, 25 pounds will be placed on the applicant’s shoulders for the stair
climb to simulate carrying a high-rise pack.
   (F)   The physical ability test shall consist of 11 separate events.
Applicants must successfully complete the first ten events within the required
time of 10:30. Applicants shall be scored according to their finish in the
timed events. That time shall include the total time and additions for any
penalties. The test time shall start when the high-rise pack bundle is picked
up off the ground. Warnings shall be assessed a five second addition of time to
the finish time of the applicant. The last event shall be the aerial climb. The
applicant shall have a maximum of ten minutes to rehab with the applicant
receiving approval after vitals to complete the aerial climb. The applicant
shall have ten minutes to complete the aerial climb once they begin. This event
will be scored as a pass/fail event.
   (G)   The physical ability test shall consist of the following skills.
      (1)   High rise pack carry. This event is designed to simulate the
critical tasks of climbing stairs in full protective clothing and carrying a
high-rise pack. An extra 25 pounds of weight shall be placed on the shoulders
of the applicant to simulate the weight of a high-rise pack and an actual high-
rise bundle of hose consisting of 50 feet of two and one- half inch hose in a
bundle, prior to the start of the event. The stairs will be three floors in
height. Once the applicant reaches the top of the stairs the 25-pound weight
shall be removed, and the hose bundle placed in the designated area. The
applicant may skip stairs on the way up the stairs. Failure to complete the
scenario or allowing the hose bundle to hit the ground other than the
designated area will result in failure of the examination.
      (2)   Hose hoist. This event is designed to simulate the critical task of
raising needed equipment to upper floors. The event is completed at the top of
a platform, three floors from the ground. Applicants must stand in a designated
area while using a rope to hoist a section of rolled hose. The rope shall
consist of five-eighths inch diameter rope and the rolled section of hose shall
be a 50-foot roll of two and one-half inch hose. The event is completed when
the hose clears the railing and is placed in the designated area. The applicant
will then proceed down the stairs to the next event. All steps must be touched,
and handrails used on the way down the stairs. Losing control and dropping the
hose and it strikes the ground shall result in a failure of the examination.
Wrapping the rope around your hand, letting the rope slip, not placing the rope
or hose in the proper are when finished, running down the stairs and failure to
use the stair handrails shall result in warnings to the applicant.
   (3)   Rescue drag. This event is designed to simulate the critical task of
removing a victim or injured firefighter from a fire scene. The event starts at
the rescue mannequin. Applicants shall grasp a 165- pound mannequin by the
handles on the shoulders of a harness, drag the mannequin 50 feet, make a 180
degree turn around a designated object, and back to the start. The event is
completed when the feet of the mannequin cross the finish line. Dropping and
losing control of the mannequin or the mannequin contacting the object you are
pulling it around will result in a failure of the examination.
      (4)   Equipment carry. This event is designed to simulate the critical
task of removing power tools from the apparatus, carrying them to the emergency
scene, and returning them to the apparatus. The event starts at the tool
compartment simulator. Applicants shall remove two saws, one at a time, from
the compartment and place them on the ground. The saws shall be one chain saw
and one K-12 saw. The applicant shall then pick up both saws, carry them 50
feet, complete a 180 degree turn around a designated object, and return to the
starting point. Both saws shall be placed on the ground, and returned, one at a
time, to the simulated tool compartment. The event is complete when both saws
are back in the compartment, in their original position. Dropping any of the
equipment will result in a failure of the examination. Allowing the equipment
to strike the object you are walking around will result in warnings to the
applicant.
      (5)   Hose drag. This event is designed to simulate the critical task of
dragging an uncharged hose from the apparatus to a designated area, and then
pulling the hose line around an object while kneeling. The event starts at the
nozzle end of a 200-foot one and three-fourths inch uncharged hose line.
Applicants must grasp the nozzle, place the hose line over their shoulder, drag
the line to the designated object, turn 90 degrees and continue to a marked
area. After reaching the designated area, the applicant must drop to at least
one knee and proceed to pull 50 feet of the hose into the designated area. The
event is completed when the 50-foot mark crosses the line of the designated
area. The applicant must remain in the designated area. Running is permitted
during this event. Dropping the hose during this event will result in failure
of the examination. Not staying in the designated area will result in warnings
to the applicant.
      (6)   Ladder extension. This event is designed to simulate the critical
task of extending a ladder to a roof or window. The event starts at a
designated area at the bottom of a 24-foot extension ladder. Applicants must
stand in the designated area while using a hand over hand method until the fly
section of the ladder is fully extended to the stops of the ladder. The fly
section will then be lowered, using the hand over hand method, back to the
starting position. Losing control of the fly section and letting the fly
section drop will result in failure of the examination. Letting the rope slip
or wrapping the rope around your hands will result in warnings to the
applicant.
      (7)   Ladder raise. This event is designed to simulate the critical task
of raising a ladder against a building. The event starts at the top rung of a
35-foot ladder, lying flat on the ground. Applicants must lift the end of the
ladder and walk the ladder up against the building. This shall be completed
using the hand over hand method, touching each rung of the ladder. Using the
side rails (beams) of the ladder will not be permitted. The event is complete
when the ladder is up against the wall. Dropping the ladder will result in
failure of the examination. Not utilizing the hand over hand method and
skipping rungs will result in warnings to the applicant.
      (8)   Forcible entry/ventilation. This event is designed to simulate the
critical task of using an axe to cut a hole for ventilation at a structure fire
incident. The event starts at a weighted sled. Applicants shall use a nine-
pound shot hammer to drive a 165-pound steel beam a horizontal distance of five
feet. Pushing, raking or hooking the beam to move it are not permitted. The
event is complete when the steel beam reaches the five-foot mark. Losing
control and dropping the hammer, pushing or pulling the sled will result in a
failure of the examination. Hitting the handle of the hammer and not placing
the hammer in the designated area when finished will result in warnings to the
applicant. Tape shall be placed near the head of the hammer for each applicant
and marks are assessed with damage to the tape. Each strike to the handle shall
constitute a warning to the applicant.
      (9)   Search. This event simulates the critical task of searching an area
with limited visibility and on an unpredictable surface. The event starts at
the search maze entrance. Applicants must enter on the bottom of the prop and
exit on the top of the prop passing through a confined area with reduced
visibility. The search maze prop shall be approximately 24 feet in length and
consist of a bottom and top level, each being two feet by two feet. The prop
shall be straight, with no bends or turns. The event is completed upon exiting
the maze. Failure of the applicant to complete the event will result in a
failure of the examination. Not entering or exiting the prop as instructed will
result in warnings to the applicant.
      (10)   Ceiling breach and pull. This event simulates the critical task of
breaching and pulling a ceiling to check for fire extension. This event is
completed at the pike pole simulator. Applicants, standing in a designated area
and using a pike pole, shall fully push up on the prop three times, then using
the pike pole hook pull down on the device five times. The event is completed
when four sets of three pushes and five pulls have been completed. The
applicant shall then exit the simulator and proceed to the finish line. Falling
off the prop, dropping the pike pole or the pike pole striking the ground will
result in failure of the examination. Time is stopped when the applicant
crosses the finish line.
      (11)   Aerial ladder climb. This event evaluates the applicant’s ability
to climb and work from heights. This event is held utilizing a 100-foot aerial
ladder, set at a 70-degree climbing angle, with the rungs aligned. Applicants
shall be placed in a safety harness and attached to a safety line during the
event. The applicant must touch the top rung of the aerial ladder. This event
shall be completed after the applicant receives medical clearance from on-scene
resources. The applicant shall start the aerial climb within ten minutes of
finishing the course and will have ten minutes to complete the event once
starting. Failure of the applicant to complete the 100-foot climb will result
in a failure of the examination.
   (H)   The applicant shall complete the evaluation with all articles of
clothing or equipment you start the test with. Time will continue until the
applicant and all items they began the test with, cross the finish line in the
same orientation you began the test in. Example: shoes on, gloves on, helmet
on. The following are examples of other actions that could result in a warning
or failure of the applicant:
      (1)   Running during the test except where permitted will result in a
warning;
      (2)   The applicant not staying on the designated path will result in a
warning;
      (3)   Not completing any portion of the evaluation will result in a
failure;
      (4)   Loss of helmet, gloves or vest during any event will result in a
warning;
      (5)   Loss of a shoe or clothing article will result in a warning and the
applicant must secure the item properly before proceeding on with the
evaluation. Time will not stop for this issue;
      (6)   Completing the test without your gloves, helmet or vest results in
a failure of the applicant; and
      (7)   Times more than 10:30 results in a failure of the applicant. During
the evaluation, if the time exceeds 10:30, the applicant shall be stopped and
removed from the course.
   (I)   The physical ability test shall be scored using a point value system
consisting of a maximum of 50 points possible. Applicants do not need to attain
a 70% minimum to continue in the process. Failure to complete any portion of
the testing or having a finish time greater than 10:30 will result in the
removal of the applicant from consideration for employment.
   (J)   The following shall be used in grading of applicants for the physical
ability test. All times shall include the applicants course time and added time
for warnings the applicant received. The scoring is as follows:
Time Earned Points

§ 33.24 EDUCATION.
   (A)   The Fire Chief and the Human Resources Director shall assign education
points after a comparison of each applicant with the educational requirements
of the job description. Education in related fields will be recognized as any
degree in Fire Science, Arson Investigation, Fire Administration or Fire Rescue
Technology.
   (B)   Education points shall be awarded as follows:
      (1)   One point: Associate Degree in fire science or related field;
      (2)   Two points: Bachelor’s Degree in fire science or related field;
      (3)   Three points: Master’s Degree in fire science or related field.
(Prior Code, § 33.19) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.25 BACKGROUND CHECK.
   Each applicant shall be required to complete a detailed personal history
questionnaire (PHQ) and shall be subject to a comprehensive personal background
investigation conducted by a person designated by the Fire Chief who is trained
to conduct such investigation. The designated investigator may contact
references indicated on the PHQ and employment application and the references
personal evaluation of the applicant shall be noted. Further investigation
shall be made relating to each applicant’s criminal and driving records,
educational background, credit standing, military history, possession of an
official Kentucky Fire Commission CPAT certification card and the like, and any
other relevant information discovered during the investigation, or which might
relate to the applicant’s qualification for the position applied for. Such
investigation shall be continued until all elements of the personal background
have been verified or disproved. The investigator may prepare a written record
of all findings, which shall be reviewed and evaluated. The Fire Chief shall
make a recommendation to the City Manager as to the applicant’s fitness for the
position applied for.
(Prior Code, § 33.20) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.26 GENERAL INTERVIEW.
   The interview allows a maximum of 30 points. There is no minimum, however,
each interviewer shall mark candidates as acceptable or not acceptable. The
City Manager shall review the interview sheets marked not acceptable. Unless
the City Manager overrules the not acceptable recommendation for just cause, no
such candidate shall be recommended for hire. Members of the Interview Board
shall have full access to all employment information for use during the
interview. The General Interview Board shall consist of a board designated by
the Fire Chief. A member from Human Resources will facilitate the general
interview.
(Prior Code, § 33.21) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.27 MILITARY SERVICE.
   Two points shall be added to the total score for each candidate who has
served a minimum of two years in any branch of the United States military and
received an honorable discharge.
(Prior Code, § 33.22) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.28 CITY RESIDENCY.
   Two points shall be added to the total score for each candidate who has
established residency within the city limits.
(Prior Code, § 33.23) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.29 POINTS AND RANKING.
   (A)   As soon as practical after the completion of §§
33.20 through
33.28 of this subchapter, the Human Resources Director shall prepare a list of
remaining applicants. They will be listed in order of highest point value
earned to lowest point value earned during the testing process.
   (B)   The top three applicants may be considered for a position. The Fire
Chief may interview the top three applicants on the eligibility list or may
elect to review the information for each of the top three applicants. The Fire
Chief shall have access to all information on the candidates gathered during
the process. The Fire Chief along with Human Resources, shall determine how
many applicants are selected for the chief officer interview. The remaining
applicants shall be ranked and placed on an eligibility list (see §
33.31 for guidance).
(Prior Code, § 33.24) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.30 CHIEF OFFICER INTERVIEW.
   Once an applicant has been selected, they shall complete the chief officer
interview. The Chief Officer Interview Board shall consist of at least three
chief officers (Fire Chief, Deputy Chief, Battalion Chiefs) designated by the
Fire Chief from the Ashland Fire Department. A member from Human Resources will
facilitate the chief officer interview. Applicants will be interviewed based on
the information from their background to determine knowledge, skills, abilities
and motivation for the position of firefighter.
(Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.31 CONDITIONAL OFFER OF EMPLOYMENT/ELIGIBILITY LIST.
   (A)   The Fire Chief may then recommend one of the applicants for employment
to the City Manager. The City Manager may authorize a conditional offer of
employment to be given to the applicant pending the results of the remaining
sections listed in the hiring process. Once all testing is completed, the City
Manager may recommend the applicant to the Board of Commissioners for final
approval.
   (B)   The eligibility list will remain effective for one year from the date
the first applicant is appointed, or until the City Manager determines that a
new eligibility list shall be created, whichever is shorter. The Fire Chief,
with the City Manager’s approval, may request to extend the eligibility list
beyond one year. The applicant shall also agree to repeat any or all portions
of the initial hiring process as determined by the Fire Chief or his or her
designee.
   (C)   To qualify for the eligibility list the applicant shall agree to
affirmatively notify the city of any change of circumstances, personal
information or facts stated on the application.
   (D)   The name of the applicant shall be removed from the eligibility list
after appointment to a position, or after refusing an appointment to a
position, or after it becomes known that an applicant has engaged in fraud or
made a misstatement of material fact on the application form and/or
examination, or after the list has expired, or after the City Manager
determines a new list be created.
(Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.32 CANDIDATE PHYSICAL ABILITY TEST (CPAT).
   As per KRS 95A.040, any applicant must complete a candidate physical ability
test (CPAT), within one year prior to the date of appointment, unless already
employed in a career fire department. A candidate cannot be appointed without
holding a valid CPAT card. The hiring packet given to candidates at the onset
of this hiring process, shall prescribe a date that the candidate will need to
provide a valid CPAT card.
(Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.33 MEDICAL PHYSICAL EXAMINATION.
   (A)   Each applicant who successfully passes all written, physical aptitude,
oral interviews, CPAT, and is offered a conditional offer of employment must
meet the following minimum physical examination standards prior to appointment
as a probationary firefighter.
   (B)   The required physical examination shall include, but is not limited
to:
      (1)   Chest x-ray;
      (2)   Electrocardiogram;
      (3)   Audiometric exam;
      (4)   Pulmonary function studies;
      (5)   Visual acuity testing;
      (6)   CBC, blood chemistry profile and HIV testing;
      (7)   TB skin (unless history of previous positive testing);
      (8)   SCBA fit testing; and
      (9)   Urine drug screen.
   (C)   The findings of the medical history/physical examination, and the
preceding listed tests, should be compatible with performance of the mental and
physical demands as listed in the job description for firefighter. Placement of
an employee whose condition or history indicates other than normal health
should not put the employee, fellow workers or the public at any increased risk
of injury or health detriment.
   (D)   The examiner shall express his or her opinion in writing as to whether
the applicant is physically fit for duty as a firefighter. Conditions which are
of questionable etiology are to be referred to the prospective employee’s
personal physician for further evaluation prior to any medical clearance being
issues. The results and diagnosis from an employee’s personal physician may be
utilized in determining the fitness for placement.
   (E)   When the applicant(s) is (are) given the conditional offer of
employment and does (do) not successfully complete the medical physical
examination, the conditional offer of employment shall be withdrawn, and the
applicant(s) shall no longer be considered for employment. The Fire Chief shall
follow the procedure detailed in §
33.30 and recommend an applicant to the City Manager for a conditional offer of
employment. This process shall continue until qualified applicants have met all
requirements, the eligibility list has been depleted, expired or a decision is
made not to fill the position.
(Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.34 POLYGRAPH.
   Each applicant will be required to complete a polygraph examination, which
shall be conducted by a polygraph examiner selected by the city.
(Prior Code, § 33.25) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.35 PSYCHOLOGICAL EVALUATION.
   Each applicant shall be required to complete a psychological evaluation.
This evaluation shall use testing procedures that are valid, constructive and
nondiscriminatory. Candidates may also be screened by a qualified professional
psychologist or psychiatrist who will provide a report to the Fire Chief on the
candidate’s fitness for duty.
(Prior Code, § 33.16) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.36 RECOMMENDATION FOR PROBATIONARY APPOINTMENT.
   (A)   Once the candidate has successfully completed appropriate testing
after the conditional offer of employment, the City Manager may recommend the
candidate to the Board of Commissioners for probationary appointment to the
Fire Department. After the Board of Commissioner’s vote, the candidate will be
notified of the results.
   (B)   Each applicant selected shall enter city service as a probationary
firefighter and shall serve a probationary period of one year, as herein
prescribed, with all pay, benefits and allowances pertinent thereto. This
probation can be extended at the discretion of the Fire Chief.
   (C)   The candidate shall perform, to the best of his or her ability, all
duties assigned to him or her and shall be subject to the same disciplinary
measures as every other member of the Ashland Fire Department, including, but
not limited to, written or oral reprimand, suspension and termination of
employment.
(Prior Code, § 33.27) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.37 TERMINATION OF EMPLOYMENT DURING THE PROBATIONARY PERIOD.
   Any probationary firefighter may be terminated from employment at any time
during the one year probationary period of employment or have their
probationary period extended at the discretion of the Fire Chief, with approval
of the City Manager and the Board of Commissioners, for any valid reason,
including, but not limited to, the following:
   (A)   Inability to perform duties in a progressive manner;
   (B)   Physical or emotional incapacity;
   (C)   Inability to assimilate education and training;
   (D)   Conduct unbecoming a firefighter;
   (E)   Public drunkenness by alcohol or any type of intoxicant, on or off
duty;
   (F)   Improper or illegal use of a vehicle or equipment;
   (G)   Insubordination;
   (H)   Negligence or incompetence;
   (I)   Any reason which demonstrates a member’s undesirable character or lack
of integrity; and
   (J)   Any other reason, which reflects negatively or with dishonor on the
city or its Fire Department.
(Prior Code, § 33.28) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
§ 33.38 CAREER APPOINTMENT.
   Upon the satisfactory completion of one year of service with the Ashland
Fire Department as a probationary firefighter pursuant to the terms and
conditions set forth in this subchapter, and upon the recommendation of the
Fire Chief, and approval from the City Manager, such probationary firefighter
shall be awarded career status with all pay, benefits and allowances pertinent
thereto.
(Prior Code, § 33.29) (Ord. 172, 2024, passed 10-25-2024)
HAZARDOUS MATERIALS EMERGENCY RESPONSE PLAN
§ 33.50 PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES.
   (A)   Purpose. The purpose of the Hazardous Materials Response Plan is to
establish an organization to mitigate hazardous materials incidents within the
city.
   (B)   Objectives.
      (1)   To describe operational concepts, organization and support systems
required to implement the plan;
      (2)   To identify authority, responsibilities, and actions of federal,
state, local and private industry agencies necessary to minimize damage to
human health, natural systems, and property and to aid in mitigating the
hazard;
      (3)   To establish an operational structure that has the ability to
function in case of hazardous materials incidents;
      (4)   To utilize Fire Department officers and members who have been
trained to handle hazardous materials incidents;
      (5)   To establish lines of authority and management for hazardous
materials incidents; and
      (6)   To establish financial responsibilities and cost recovery
procedures.
(Prior Code, § 33.60) (Ord. 78, passed 6-2-1994)
§ 33.51 INCIDENT CLASSIFICATIONS.
   (A)   The basis used for determining the level of a hazardous material
incident are:
      (1)   Level of technical expertise required to abate the incident;
      (2)   Extent of municipal, county, and state government involvement;
      (3)   Extent of evacuation of civilians;
      (4)   Extent of injuries or death; and
      (5)   Extent and involvement of decontamination procedures.
   (B)   There are three levels of hazardous materials incident
classifications:
      (1)   Level I incidents.
         (a)   Spills, leaks, ruptures or fires involving hazardous materials
that can be contained, extinguished or abated utilizing equipment, supplies and
resources immediately available to the City Fire Department; or
         (b)   Hazardous material incidents that do not require evacuation of
civilians.
      (2)   Level II incidents. (The officer in charge of a Level I incident
may upgrade the incident to a Level II incident.)
         (a)   Hazardous materials incidents that can only be identified,
tested, sampled, contained, extinguished or abated utilizing the resources of
the City Fire Department’s special response unit; a hazardous materials
incidents that require the use of chemical-protective gear and specialized
equipment;
         (b)   Hazardous materials incidents that require evacuation of
civilians within the area of the City Fire Department; or
         (c)   Fires involving hazardous materials that are permitted to burn
for a controlled period of time or allowed to consume themselves.
      (3)   Level III incidents. (The officer in charge of a Level II incident
may upgrade the incident to a Level III incident.)
         (a)   Spills, leaks or ruptures that can be contained or abated
utilizing the highly specialized equipment and supplies available to
environmental or industrial response personnel;
         (b)   Fires involving hazardous materials that are allowed to burn due
to the ineffectiveness or dangers of the use of extinguishing agents or the
unavailability of water; and/or there is a real threat of larger container
failure; and/or an explosion, detonation, BLEVE or container failure has
occurred;
         (c)   Hazardous material incidents that require evacuation of
civilians extending across jurisdictional boundaries, and/or there are serious
civilian injuries or deaths as a result of the hazardous material incident;
         (d)   Hazardous material incidents requiring decontamination of
civilians or personnel; or
         (e)   Hazardous material incidents that have become one of multi-
agency involvement of large proportions.
(Prior Code, § 33.61) (Ord. 78, passed 6-2-1994)
§ 33.52 INCIDENT COMMAND AND SCENE MANAGEMENT.
   (A)   The Incident Commander (IC) shall be the designated Fire Department
officer responsible for mitigating the hazards at the scene of a hazardous
materials incident. Upon arrival, he or she shall secure and maintain immediate
control until the situation has been abated.
   (B)   The City Fire Department shall accept and provide the position of
Incident Commander for the scene of all hazardous materials incidents within
the city limits. The City Fire Department shall coordinate and direct within
its control all Fire Department activities within its jurisdiction, and
responsibility to include, but not be limited to, rescue, first aid, product
identification, scene stabilization and management, suppression activities,
protection of exposures, containment, agency notification, scene isolation,
personnel protection and decontamination.
   (C)   The Incident Commander shall employ overall management and
coordination of a hazardous materials incident. The Incident Commander shall be
responsible for the identification of the incident resources and needs, the
procurement of these resources, and the coordination of the resources, so as to
abate the incident and protect life, property and the environment.
(Prior Code, § 33.62) (Ord. 78, passed 6-2-1994)
§ 33.53 CONTROL ZONES.
   (A)   Responsibility. The Incident Commander shall be responsible for set-up
of four zones surrounding any hazardous materials incident.
   (B)   Cold zone. This zone shall include the command post. This zone shall
be of a safe distance from the hazardous materials incident but shall provide a
view of the incident if possible.
   (C)   Warm zone. The WARM ZONE shall be defined as an area where some
potential or real danger exists to the public or the environment.
Identification of the warm zone shall be done by the first arriving Fire
Department company officer. Access shall be limited to those members or
agencies on scene who are appropriately protected and directly engaged in
rescue, control and preliminary stabilization measures.
   (D)   Hot zone. The hot zone shall be designated as necessary to identify
and define an area of exceptional danger, including extreme threat to life
safety. Identification of the hot zone shall be done by the first arriving
company officer. This zone may be expanded at any time by the Incident
Commander. Access shall be controlled by the IC. Only personnel designated and
of necessity will be allowed access.
   (E)   Decontamination zone. The decontamination zone will be designated as
necessary to establish a procedure to decontaminate personnel, civilians and
equipment in an effort to reduce or stop the spread of suspected contaminants.
Identification and set up of the decontamination zone shall be the
responsibility of the IC. Access to the decontamination zone of contaminated
people shall be controlled by a Decontamination Officer. Only the
Decontamination Officer may allow anyone to exit the decontamination zone. All
workers in the decontamination zone shall be properly protected at all times.
(Prior Code, § 33.63) (Ord. 78, passed 6-2-1994)
§ 33.54 OPERATIONAL PLAN ACTIVATION.
   This plan will become operational when the City Fire Department receives
notification of any hazardous materials incident.
(Prior Code, § 33.64) (Ord. 78, passed 6-2-1994)
§ 33.55 IMMEDIATE ON-SCENE ACTIONS.
   (A)   Identification.
      (1)   The first Fire Department officer to arrive on the scene will
attempt to identify:
         (a)   The type of material involved;
         (b)   The quantity of material involved;
         (c)   The possibility of contamination; and
         (d)   The immediate exposure problem.
      (2)   This information shall be transmitted to dispatch immediately.
   (B)   Level I. If the Fire Department officer determines that the incident
is Level I, he or she will proceed to mitigate the problem.
   (C)   Level II or III.
      (1)   If the Fire Department officer determines that the incident is a
Level II or III, he or she shall take whatever action is necessary to control
the incident within the capability of his or her personnel, resources and
equipment.
      (2)   The Fire Department officer first on the scene will inform incoming
companies of his or her evaluation and the actions he or she is taking and
shall direct responding units on which access routes they should use when
approaching the incident.
      (3)   The first arriving officer shall initiate steps to identify and
establish the warm zone.
   (D)   Command post. The first arriving company officer shall establish a
command post in the most strategically desirable and safe location. A chief
officer shall assume command upon his or her arrival.
   (E)   Base. A base shall be established as necessary outside the anticipated
hazard area in a removed and safe location. This area and its resources will be
coordinated by assigned personnel. The base location is to be transmitted to
RPSCC as soon as possible, and all responding units dispatched to this incident
shall be directed to report to base.
   (F)   Communications. At the direction of the Incident Commander, all units
on the scene shall be directed to switch to fire F-2 radio channel. The IC
shall continue to monitor F-1.
   (G)   Incident stabilization. It shall be the responsibility of the IC to
identify the problem, to determine the possible course of action that could
happen as a result of this incident, and to record this information. The IC
shall evaluate this information, and will determine the best course of action
to take to mitigate the hazard. The IC may request that the incident be
upgraded to Level III.
   (H)   Evacuation. If evacuation is necessary the IC shall notify the
appropriate law enforcement agencies. The law enforcement agency having
jurisdiction, assisted by other appropriate agencies, shall plan and conduct an
orderly evacuation within a specified geographical area. Utilization of the
news media to assist in notifying the public of an evacuation will be the
responsibility of the IC.
   (I)   Clean-up and disposal.
      (1)   The primary responsibility for the assumption of all costs for the
clean-up and disposal of a chemical shall be:
         (a)   The person or persons whose negligent or willful act caused such
spill, release or potential spill or release of a hazardous material;
         (b)   The person or persons who own or had custody of the chemical or
hazardous material or waste at the time of the spill or release; and
         (c)   The person or persons who owned or had custody or control of
container or transport vehicle that held such chemical or hazardous material or
waste.
      (2)   The Incident Commander shall identify the responsible party. When,
in the opinion of the IC, the substance must be cleaned up according to OSHA,
EPA or other governmental organization, the responsible party or its
representative shall call a reputable and licensed hazardous waste hauler for
clean-up disposal.
      (3)   The City Fire Department is authorized to clean-up or abate any
chemical, hazardous material or waste released or deposited upon or into any
property within the city, in the event the responsible party cannot be located
or identified, or refuses to cooperate.
      (4)   The persons described in division (I)(1) of this section shall be
liable to the city for all costs incurred as a result of response,
investigation, mitigation and clean-up of hazardous materials releases or
potential releases thereof. Payment for the above services must be received by
the city within 30 days. Payments made after 30 days shall incur a penalty of
5% per month.
      (5)   It shall not be the responsibility of the city to remove any
hazardous material. The Incident Commander shall remain on scene until arrival
of the appropriate and approved agency. The IC shall oversee the clean-up
operation in an advisory capacity to insure that removal of product and
containers are done so correctly and safely.
(Prior Code, § 33.65) (Ord. 78, passed 6-2-1994)
§ 33.56 COST RECOVERY.
   (A)   In the event that the city ultimately must pay for clean-up and
removal of a hazardous material, the City Fire Department may pursue all
appropriate legal avenues to initiate action against the spiller to recover all
costs incurred.
   (B)   All supporting agencies shall assist the city in initiating action to
recover all cost incurred in the handling of the hazardous materials incident.
(Prior Code, § 33.66)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 34.01 ADOPTION OF STATE LAW RELATIVE TO FIRE AND POLICE PENSION SYSTEMS.
   (A)   The provisions of KRS 79.080 are hereby included and incorporated into
the framework of the city’s pension system relating to members of the Police
and Fire Divisions of the city, which pension system is not regulated pursuant
to KRS 95.852.
   (B)   The following excerpt from KRS 79.080 is included herein: “Any plan
adopted shall provide that any officer or member of a paid Fire or Police
Department who has completed five years or more as a member of the Department,
but who is unable to perform his or her duties by reason of heart disease or
any disease of the lungs or respiratory tract, is presumed to have contracted
his or her disease while on active duty as a result of strain or the inhalation
of noxious fumes, poison or gases, and shall be retired by the Pension Board
under terms of the pension system of which he or she is a member, if the member
passed an entrance physical examination and was found to be in good health as
required.”
(Prior Code, § 34.01) (Ord. 4-1971, passed 3-8-1971)
§ 34.02 POLICE REGULATIONS ADOPTED BY REFERENCE.
   The Rules and Regulations of the Police Department, Ashland, Kentucky, being
a document separate and apart from this section, is hereby adopted in full, by
reference, as an ordinance of the city, as fully to all intents and purposes as
if set out at length herein. A copy of the document entitled Rules and
Regulations of the Police Department, Ashland, Kentucky, and including
amendments from time to time, shall be kept on file in the office of the City
Clerk/Human Resources Director, and shall be made available for reference at
all times during the regular office hours of that office.
(Prior Code, § 34.02) (Ord. 205, 2024, passed 12-12-2024; Ord. 11, 2015, passed
2-11-2025)
§ 34.03 PAYMENT OF POLICE PERSONNEL FOR COURT APPEARANCES.
   (A)   All personnel of the Police Department non-exempt shall hereafter be
compensated for off-duty appearances before any judicial body arising out of
their employment with the city, said judicial bodies to include Boyd Circuit
Court, Juvenile Court, Boyd District Court and in any other judicial
proceedings for which the employee was subpoenaed or summoned in the following
manner.
      (1)   If the appearance requires four hours or more, including travel
time, waiting time and actual appearance, said compensation shall be based upon
the hours actually incurred.
      (2)   If the appearance requires less than four hours, including travel
time, waiting time and actual appearance, said compensation shall be payment
for four hours.
      (3)   All payments shall be based on an hourly charge equivalent to the
salary schedule of the involved personnel.
      (4)   Certification of the time expended shall be made by said personnel
to the Chief of Police. Payment shall be made after approval by the Chief of
Police.
   (B)   This section shall not affect, in any manner, court appearances on
days upon which the personnel was regularly scheduled to work, and no
additional pay shall be received for court appearances on said on-duty days,
except that personnel attending judicial proceedings immediately prior to or
immediately after a regularly scheduled tour of duty shall be compensated for
that time only at the normal hourly overtime rate as prescribed by Kentucky
Revised Statutes. Such compensation shall not exceed the compensation method
described in division (A) above.
(Prior Code, § 34.03) (Ord. 49-1997, passed 4-17-1997)
§ 34.04 LAW ENFORCEMENT FOUNDATION PROGRAM.
   (A)   The city hereby declares its intention to continue to participate in
the Law Enforcement Foundation Program established by KRS 15.410 through 15.520
and 15.990, as amended (training incentive program).
   (B)   It is the intention of the Board of Commissioners that all provisions
and requirements of KRS 15.410 through 15.520 and 15.990, as amended, and of
this section as amended from time to time, be employed as guidelines for the
implementation of the Law Enforcement Foundation Program, as defined herein.
   (C)   Each officer of the City Police Division shall be paid from city funds
an annual salary, based on a standard work year, as shall be determined from
time to time by the Board of Commissioners.
   (D)   Qualifications and training for police officers shall meet the
qualifications and training requirements of KRS 15.382, as certified by the
Kentucky Law Enforcement Council.
   (E)   No officer shall have his or her base salary reduced or be denied a
normal salary increase to which he or she is otherwise entitled because of the
salary incentive payments provided by the State Crime Commission under KRS
15.410 through 15.520.
   (F)   The Police Division and each officer thereof shall comply with all
provisions of law applicable to local police, including the transmission of
data to the Bureau of Criminal Information and Statistics, as required by KRS
17.150. The Police Division and each officer thereof shall further comply with
all reasonable rules and regulations, appropriate to the size and location of
the local Police Division, issued by the State Crime Commission to facilitate
the administration of the Law Enforcement Foundation Fund and further the
purposes of KRS 15.410 through 15.520.
   (G)   The Chief of Police shall prepare or cause to be prepared any
quarterly and other reports as may be reasonably required by the State Crime
Commission to facilitate administration of the Law Enforcement Foundation Fund
and further the purposes of KRS 15.410 through 15.520.
   (H)   The Director of Finance shall deposit in an appropriate account, which
can be identified separately from all other sources, all monies received under
KRS 15.410 through 15.520. Forthwith upon receipt of any monies under KRS
15.410 through 15.520, the Director of Finance shall pay to each police officer
the full amount received on behalf of that officer, giving to each officer a
check stub or receipt on which the gross amount of monies paid to him or her
under KRS 15.410 through 15.520 is included and identified. All financial
records relating to monies received under KRS 15.410 through 15.520 shall be
retained for a period of three years and until the completion of an audit
approved by the State Crime Commission and the Federal Law Enforcement
Assistance Administration.
(Prior Code, § 34.04) (Ord. 12-1973, passed 4-3-1973; Ord. 28-1974, passed 7-

7-1981; Ord. 21-1982, passed 4-15-1982)
HIRING REGULATIONS
§ 34.15 INTRODUCTION.
   (A)   The procedures and requirements for recruitment, selection,
employment, training and evaluation of entry level police officers with the
rank of officer for the Department of Police (also referred to herein as the
“Police Department”) of the City of Ashland, Kentucky, shall be hereafter
prescribed in this subchapter or any future amending or superseding ordinance
thereto. Each officer of the Ashland Police Department shall be bound by the
requirements of this subchapter and shall be subject to the rules, regulations,
general orders and special orders of the Ashland Police Department.
   (B)   This subchapter shall be known and may be referred to as the
“Comprehensive Hiring Ordinance for Police Officers for the Department of
Police of the City of Ashland”.
   (C)   For the purpose of this subchapter, those words, terms or phrases used
herein in the masculine gender shall include the feminine gender, and those
words, terms or phrases used herein in the feminine gender shall include the
masculine gender, except where the usage clearly indicates otherwise.
(Prior Code, § 34.20) (Ord. 174, 2022, passed 11-17-2022; Ord. 86, 2023, passed
6-23-2023)
§ 34.16 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter and §§
34.45 through
34.55, the following definitions shall apply unless the context clearly
indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CAREER STATUS POLICE OFFICER. A police officer who has completed his or her
required probationary period of employment and has been approved as required by
this subchapter or amending or superseding ordinances and has been appointed to
career status pursuant to the terms of §
34.54.
   COACH-ADVISER. A career status police officer to whom a probationary police
officer is assigned for on the job training and guidance.
   DATE OF APPOINTMENT. The date upon which a probationary police officer
begins employment and takes the oath of office.
   DEPARTMENT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE TRAINING (DOCJT). A Department of the
Kentucky Justice Cabinet as established by KRS 15A.020 and as amended, for the
purpose of providing training to police officers.
   DUTY SERGEANT. Any on-duty police sergeant assigned to a patrol team.
   FIELD OPERATIONS DIVISION COMMANDER. A police major assigned to command the
entire field operations division.
   KENTUCKY CERTIFIED PEACE OFFICER. A person that meets all legal requirements
for and is therefore entitled to the classification as a certified police
officer in the Commonwealth of Kentucky responsive of the stipulations of KRS
15.380 to 15.402.
   KENTUCKY LAW ENFORCEMENT COUNCIL (KLEC). An independent administrative body
of state government made up of the Attorney General, law enforcement department
heads throughout the Commonwealth of Kentucky, members of higher education and
a city manager or mayor, a member of the Kentucky State Bar Association and a
citizen of Kentucky not coming without the previous classifications. The
Council is vested with the powers to prescribe standards for law enforcement
training required under KRS 15.310 to 15.510 and KRS 15.990 to 15.992, along
with other functions.
   NON-CERTIFIED PEACE OFFICER APPLICANTS. A person that has made application
to the City of Ashland for employment as a police officer that is not a
Kentucky certified peace officer as defined under KRS 15.380 to 15.404.
   POINT VALUE. Numerical value of ratings assigned for completion of certain
sections of this subchapter, which describe the selection process.
   POLICE OFFICER TRAINING COORDINATOR. A command officer that has been charged
with coordinating schedules, activities and plans associated for on the job
training and guidance.
   POLICE TRAINEE. This is a non-sworn, training-level classification in the
city’s police service. Incumbents are hired from an entry-level eligibility
list and are sent to the Department of Criminal Justice Training (DOCJT) for
basic police academy training. During training, incumbents do not have police
powers and are subject to the rules and regulations of the City of Ashland, the
Ashland Police Department, and the DOCJT. Advancement to a sworn probationary
police officer position is contingent upon successful completion of the basic
training academy and the final review of the Police Chief. Upon approval, the
officer(s) will begin a one-year probationary period.
   PROBATIONARY PERIOD. A period of one year beginning on date of appointment
as a probationary police officer and ending on first anniversary date as
probationary police officer.
   PROBATIONARY POLICE OFFICER. A police officer who has not reached the first
anniversary from his or her date of appointment as a probationary police
officer.
   RESIDENCE. That place where a person has his or her true, fixed and
permanent home and principal establishment, and to which whenever he or she is
absent, he or she has the intention of returning. This residence shall
determine where a person may exercise the privilege of voting and other legal
rights and privileges.
   SCHOOL RESOURCE OFFICER-CONTRACT RETIREE. This is a police practitioner
class responsible for the provision of a broad range of law enforcement
services to protect individual rights, preserve the peace, prevent and suppress
crime, protect life and property, identify and apprehend criminal offenders and
enforce regulatory measures in the Ashland Independent Schools System. This
position is through a contractual agreement to supply officers to the school
system as required by law. The separated officers by contract are not covered
by the city collective bargaining agreement but are to follow the city rules
and regulations, Ashland Police Department rules and regulations and Ashland
Police Department general orders along with federal and Commonwealth of
Kentucky laws. Officers of the department covered under the city collective
bargaining agreement are not in this class or eligible for the position.
   TEAM COMMANDER. A police lieutenant assigned to a group of personnel for the
purpose of accomplishing the police duties required of that group during a tour
of duty.
(Prior Code, § 34.21) (Ord. 174, 2022, passed 11-17-2022; Ord. 86, 2023, passed
6-23-2023)
§ 34.17 AUTHORIZATION FOR HIRING PROCESS; ADVERTISING REQUIREMENT.
   (A)   Upon determination by the Chief of Police that there is a need to
begin an employment process and the eligibility list (§
34.30) has expired or contains no additional qualified applicants, the City
Manager shall authorize and require the Human Resources Director to make public
by appropriate advertising the intent of the city to employ such personnel. The
Chief of Police can recommend a hiring process for certified Kentucky peace
officers only or non-certified applicants or both for processing. Basic
prerequisite qualifications for police officer and the location where
applications may be obtained will be advertised in an open and constant
application process without a closing date for receiving completed
applications. When an application process is needed, the Chief of Police will
submit for filling positions from applications that are currently on file in
the Human Resources Department. The open and constant application process will
be advertised periodically to remind any potential candidates that applications
are being taken constantly.
   (B)   The city is an equal opportunity employer without regard to race,
color, religion, ethnicity, gender, age, national origin, disability or status
as a Vietnam era veteran.
   (C)   The requirement for any documents to be attached to or presented with
the completed application shall be noted thereon.
(Prior Code, § 34.22) (Ord. 174, 2022, passed 11-17-2022; Ord. 86, 2023, passed
6-23-2023)
§ 34.18 PREREQUISITE QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS OF APPLICANTS FOR POLICE
OFFICER.
   Prior to a conditional offer of employment for the position of police
officer, each applicant must meet the following prerequisite requirements. The
applicant must:
   (A)   Be a citizen of the United States;
   (B)   By the date of submission of the application be 20 years of age per
KRS 15.382 and provide a copy of the birth certificate with application and be
21 years of age before graduating the Department of Criminal Justice Training
Academy. If an applicant is from another state that has received reciprocity,
and was certified prior to 21 years of age when the same parameters apply until
the needed training has been completed and the applicant is then Kentucky
certified as a peace officer. The certification will not be valid until the
applicant reaches the age of 21 years of age;
   (C)   Be a high school graduate or must have earned a general educational
development (GED) diploma for high school level and provide a copy of high
school/GED diploma with application. Documentation of home schooling will have
to be approved through the Kentucky Law Enforcement Council (KLEC). The KLEC
has identified educational processes and institutions they recognize for
satisfying the high school diploma requirement;
   (D)   If a veteran of any branch of the armed forces of the United States
present with his or her application a copy of official documentation, or his or
her DD214, official discharge, showing the reason for his or her discharge. The
applicant shall not have received a dishonorable discharge, bad conduct
discharge or general discharge under other than honorable conditions;
   (E)   Have any other qualifications as may be prescribed by the Constitution
of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Kentucky Statutes, K.L.E.C. Peace Officer
Professional Standards (POPS) or ordinances of the city;
   (F)   Be an orderly, law-abiding citizen of the United States with no prior
felony conviction(s); or convictions of domestic violence and is not prohibited
by federal or state law from possessing a firearm;
   (G)   Not have had certification as a peace officer revoked in Kentucky or
any other state;
   (H)   Be a person of sobriety and integrity, and of sound mind and body;
   (I)   Be willing to undergo and successfully complete thorough physical
agility tests;
   (J)   Be willing to complete a KLEC psychological suitability screener
examination, and any additional psychological examination performed by a
licensed psychologist;
   (K)   Be willing to be fingerprinted and undergo and successfully complete
thorough personal background investigation;
   (L)   After a conditional offer of employment be willing to submit to and
successfully complete polygraph testing;
   (M)   Provide a truthful statement certifying he or she has not used illicit
drugs for the past 36 months;
   (N)   As a pre-condition to employment and a condition to continued
employment, execute a waiver to submit to random testing for illicit drugs to
remain in force as long as employed by the Ashland Police Department;
   (O)   As a condition to continued employment, be willing to undergo
polygraph examination when given a lawful order to do so by an APD command
officer during the course of any departmental investigation;
   (P)   After a conditional offer of employment be willing to undergo and
successfully complete thorough medical examination;
   (Q)   Possess a valid license to operate a motor vehicle and provide a copy
of the driver’s license with the application;
   (R)   Be willing to submit to a yearly medical examination;
   (S)   Be willing to execute a repayment agreement for continued employment
with the APD for a minimum of 36 months; and effective June 29, 2023 any new
peace officer employed will execute a repayment agreement contract for the
length of 60 months (five years) as pursuant to KRS 70.290;
   (T)   Be willing to attend the DOCJT basic training academy in Richmond,
Kentucky; and
   (U)   Be free from tattoos or body piercing that will be visible while in
any departmentally issued uniform. Body piercing does not include the piercing
of the ear lobe. Officers with visible tattoos in any departmentally issued
uniform prior to August 1, 2007, shall not be required to remove the existing
tattoo, but shall not add to the tattoo or receive any additional tattoos that
would be visible in any departmentally issued uniform. Effective February 1,
2022 any tattoos, body piercing and all forms of body art will be covered as
specified but will be governed by the Chief of Police through a general order
of the Ashland Police Department. The Chief of Police will govern the policy
and adjust under his or her discretion.
(Prior Code, § 34.23) (Ord. 174. 2022, passed 11-17-2022; Ord. 86, 2023, passed
6-23-2023)
§ 34.19 RE-EMPLOYMENT.
   (A)   The purpose of this section is to allow the city to re-employ trained
qualified personnel to the ranks of the Police Department under the following
conditions:
      (1)   Applicant left city service in good standing;
      (2)   Applicant was employed for at least one year;
      (3)   Applicant meets all current employment requirements;
      (4)   Be willing to execute a repayment agreement for continued
employment with the Ashland Police Department for 60 months, pursuant to KRS
70.290;
      (5)   Re-employment has the recommendation of the City Manager, and
approval of the Board of Commissioners;
      (6)   Possess a valid license to operate a motor vehicle;
      (7)   Fingerprinted for a criminal background check;
      (8)   No prohibition on firearm possession federal or state;
      (9)   Has received and read the Kentucky Law Enforcement Officer’s Code
of Ethics;
      (10)   Interviewed by the employing agency;
      (11)   Not have certification as a peace officer permanently revoked in
another state;
      (12)   Chief of Police has communicated with head of law enforcement
agency that most recently employed the officer to determine whether he or she
left that agency due to reasons relating to unfavorable employment;
      (13)   For the purposes of the School Resource Officer contract positions
and not covered by the collective bargaining agreement, an officer retired in
good standing from a Kentucky agency and their certification for peace officer
is in good standing considering work history, training, and determination by
the Chief of Police as an acceptable candidate; and
      (14)   Retirement positions whether School Resource Officer or back to
full duty will be required to possible enter into contracts with the Ashland
Independent School District, Kentucky Public Pension Authority and the like.
   (B)   Applicants meeting the aforestated conditions will be required to
complete those steps in the testing and evaluation procedures determined by the
City Manager to be necessary and appropriate in each particular circumstance
based on previous employment history and other pertinent personal information.
   (C)   Applicants that are retired from the city’s Police Department and are
also recommended for rehire are allowable. If rehired, guidelines established
in KRS 95.022 will be followed. The law restricts the number of retired
officers within the agency. A contractual agreement (Addendum A) will be
required by all officers pertaining to KRS 95.022 which will be updated yearly.
(Prior Code, § 34.24) (Ord. 174, 2022, passed 11-17-2022; Ord. 86, 2023, passed
6-23-2023)

§ 34.22 PHYSICAL FITNESS EVALUATION.
   (A)   Physical fitness evaluation. Consistent with the implementation of the
Peace Officer Professional Standards Act, KRS 15.380 to 15.404, enacted by 1998
Ky. Acts Chapter 606, all applicants for the position of police officer shall
be required to pass a battery of physical fitness tests.
      (1)   Applicants will be required to complete a battery of tests,
consisting of a one and one- half-mile run, 300-meter run, maximum push up, one
repetition maximum bench press and one-minute sit-up.
      (2)   Applicants may be required to have a medical examination to
determine if they can safely participate in the physical agility testing. All
applicants must have Kentucky Law Enforcement Council Medical Release Form(s)
and signed by a physician if required.
      (3)   In response to legislation enacted by the 1998 Kentucky General
Assembly, KRS 15.382, the Kentucky Law Enforcement Council and the Kentucky
Department of Criminal Justice Training, established physical training
standards for pre-selection screening of peace officer applicants. The
Department conducted a validation study to determine which areas of physical
fitness are necessary to perform the job of a Kentucky peace officer, and the
level of fitness necessary to perform the essential functions of basic
training. Currently, the test battery consists of five items. Dr. Bryant
Stamford and Dr. Robert Moffatt completed the present study in the summer of
2009. This new approach employs an “overall” scoring scheme which allows a
lower score on one test item to be compensated by a higher score on another
test item.
      (4)   The evaluation is for the purpose of demonstrating physical skills
necessary to perform essential job functions and to determine as accurately as
possible the ability of the applicant to cope with the extreme physical stress
of a police officer. The evaluation shall be conducted and supervised by KLEC
staff and monitored by designee(s) of the Chief of Police. The officer
designated to perform background investigations shall express a written opinion
to the Chief of Police as to each applicant’s ability to perform physical tasks
relative to real tasks performed on the job.
      (5)   Each applicant shall receive a copy of the evaluation format a
reasonable amount of time prior to the evaluation.
   (B)   Physical fitness. Physical fitness means having the physical readiness
to perform the strenuous and critical tasks of the job. The physical fitness
areas that have been determined to be the underlying factors for an officer’s
capability to do the job consist of five specific and different areas.
      (1)   Aerobic power or cardiovascular endurance. This is having an
efficient heart and cardiovascular system so that an officer can perform
physical tasks over a sustained period of time. It is an important area for
performing job tasks such as making foot pursuits and long-term use of force
situations.
      (2)   Anaerobic power. This is having the ability to make short intense
bursts of effort. This is an important area for performing job tasks such as
short sprint pursuit situations.
      (3)   Upper body absolute strength. This is having the upper body
strength to make maximal efforts against a resistance. This is important for
performing physical tasks that require lifting, carrying and pushing.
      (4)   Upper body muscular endurance. This is having the capability to
make repeated muscular contractions with the upper body without getting
fatigued. This is important for much use of force job tasks.
      (5)   Trunk or abdominal muscular endurance. This is having the
capability to make repeated muscular contractions with the abdominal area
without getting fatigued. The abdomen is the fulcrum of the body and is
important in many tasks involving lifting, pulling and dragging.
   (C)   Measurement.
      (1)   Physical fitness will be measured during the performance of five
physical fitness tests that will be given in three hours in one day.
         (a)   One and one half-mile run. This measures aerobic power or
cardiovascular endurance (the ability to have stamina over time). This test
consists of running/walking, as fast as possible, the distance of one and one-
half miles.
         (b)   Three hundred meter run. This measures aerobic power or the
ability to make an intense burst of effort for a short time period or distance.
This test consists of sprinting 300 meters as fast as possible.
         (c)   One repetition maximum (rm) bench-press. This measures the
absolute strength of the upper body. The candidate lies on a bench and pushes
up as much weight as possible one time.
         (d)   Maximum push up test. This measures the muscular endurance of
the upper body. The candidate executes as many push-ups as possible from the
front, lean and rest position with no time limit.
         (e)   One minute sit up test. This measures the abdominal or trunk
muscular endurance. While lying on the ground, the candidate executes in one
minute as many bent leg sit ups as possible.
      (2)   The procedure and order for testing will be as follows. Five
physical fitness tests will be given in three hours, in the following order:
         (a)   Bench press (percent of body weight – conversion);
         (b)   Sit up test (one minute time limit);
         (c)   Three hundred meter run;
         (d)   Push up test (two-minute time limit); and
         (e)   One and one-half mile run.
      (3)   The following chart is used to determine the points earned for each
event. In order to meet the state standard, an overall minimum of 50 points
must be achieved. Failure to meet the overall minimum requirement constitutes a
failure for the test battery.
      (4)   Physical performance points distribution:
 
Event                       9 pts. 9.5 pts. 10 pts. 10.5 pts. 11 pts.
Bench press (% body weight) 55.3%  59.7%    64%     68.5%     73%
Sit ups (repetitions)       13     16       18      —       18
300-meter run (seconds)     68     67       65      —       65
Push-ups (repetitions)      14     17       20      23        25
1.5 mile run (min:sec)      17:56  17:54    17:12   16:44     16:15
   Rating Point Value: A total of 55 points possible
 
   (D)   Annual medical examination.
      (1)   Effective July 1, 1994, sworn officers of the Department shall
receive a comprehensive yearly medical examination at no cost to the officer.
This examination will be provided by a physician selected by the city.
Participation in this program for officers hired prior to July 1, 1994, is
voluntary.
      (2)   Each sworn officer employed after July 1, 1994, is required to
participate in the yearly medical examination. Results of the individual
medical examinations are confidential and will not be reported to the city.
Medical concerns identified by the physician will be referred to the officer
for follow-up with his or her personal physician.
(Prior Code, § 34.27) (Ord. 174, 2022, passed 11-17-2022; Ord. 86, 2023, passed
6-23-2023)

§ 34.24 SUITABILITY SCREENER, PERSONAL BACKGROUND INVESTIGATION AND POLYGRAPH
EXAMINATION.
   If not disqualified by reason of any required prior examination and
evaluation, the applicant shall be subject to a suitability screener and
polygraph examination conducted by the Kentucky Law Enforcement Council; and a
comprehensive personal background investigation which shall be conducted by the
Chief of Police or his or her appointed agent.
   (A)   Suitability screener.
      (1)   If not disqualified by reason of any required prior examination and
evaluation, the applicant shall submit to suitability screening consistent with
the Peace Officer Professional Standards Act, KRS 15.380 to 15.404, enacted by
1998 Ky. Acts Chapter 606. This screening measures a broad spectrum of
abilities, personal characteristics and related constructs such as integrity,
conscientiousness and vocational preference, which are relevant to job related
duties. Overall, the test is designed to provide additional screening
information to agency executives about an applicant’s suitability or
unsuitability to become a Kentucky peace officer.
      (2)   Applicant will be provided with web address and a password and
shall completely fill out the on-line personal history questionnaire (PHQ).
Upon completing the PHQ, the applicant will print one copy for his or her file,
one copy for the KLEC and one copy for the Ashland Police Department. The
applicant shall hand-carry the copy for the KLEC and the copy for the Ashland
Police Department to the test site on the day of the suitability screening
test. Information provided on this form should be current, not exceeding 60
days from the date of the applicant’s signature. The applicant shall also
submit a legitimate form of photo I.D. when reporting for the suitability
screener.
      (3)   There is no time limit for completing the suitability screener.
Usually the test takes anywhere from two and one-half to five hours to
complete. So as not to feel rushed, the applicant is instructed not to schedule
other activities on the day of the testing that would interfere with time
required to complete the suitability screener.
      (4)   Each applicant’s completed suitability screening test is mailed to
Law Enforcement Services, Incorporated (LESI) for review and analysis. The
suitability report addresses findings in three performance rating areas:
intellectual ability; vocational preference and background; and personality and
psychological adjustment. At the end of the report is a final statement
indicating the suitability or unsuitability of the applicant to become a
Kentucky peace officer. If applicant is considered unsuitable, he or she will
no longer be considered for the position.
   (B)   Psychological evaluation. Appointment to police trainee or
probationary police officer for a certified officer is made contingent upon the
candidate successfully passing the suitability screener administered by the
KLEC. This testing uses procedures that are valid, constructive and
nondiscriminatory. Candidates will also be screened by a qualified professional
psychologist or psychiatrist who will provide a report to the Chief of Police
on the candidate’s fitness for duty.
   (C)   Personal background investigation.
      (1)   The Chief of Police or his or her appointed agent shall contact
references indicated on the application and on the PHQ and personal evaluations
of the applicant shall be noted by the Chief of Police or his or her appointed
agent.
      (2)   Further investigation shall be made relating to the applicant’s:
         (a)   Educational background;
         (b)   Past employment history;
         (c)   Personal background as such relates to the position applied for;
         (d)   Credit standing;
         (e)   Criminal records; and
         (f)   Any other relative information discovered during the course of
investigation or which might relate to the applicant’s qualification for the
position applied for.
      (3)   Such investigation shall be continued until all elements of the
personal background investigation have been verified or disproved. The Chief of
Police or his or her appointed agent shall prepare a written record of all
findings which shall be reviewed and evaluated. The Chief of Police shall make
a recommendation to the City Manager as to the applicant’s fitness for the
position applied for.
   (D)   Polygraph. Consistent with the implementation of the Peace Officer
Professional Standards and Certification Act, each applicant shall be required
to complete a polygraph examination which shall be conducted by a polygraph
examiner provided by the KLEC. The polygraph examiner will prepare a report to
the Chief of Police.
(Prior Code, § 34.29) (Ord. 174, 2022, passed 11-17-2022; Ord. 86, 2023, passed
6-23-2023)
§ 34.25 ORAL INTERVIEW AND EVALUATION.
   (A)   Upon having satisfactorily met requirements prior to the oral
interview as set forth in this subchapter, the applicant shall meet with the
Chief of Police or his or her designee, the Human Resources Director or his or
her designee, and a career status police officer for the purpose of submitting
to an oral interview in order that those conducting the interview may better
ascertain the applicant’s qualification for the position of police officer and
of the applicant’s probability of completing all training established by the
Kentucky Justice Cabinet, DOCJT and the applicant’s probationary period of
employment.
   (B)   Persons conducting the interviews of applicants shall have at their
disposal the results of all investigations, PHQ, employment application and
documents attached thereto. The officer conducting the background investigation
shall be present during the oral interview and evaluation. The interview allows
a maximum of 30 points. There is no minimum; however, each interviewer shall
mark candidates as acceptable or not acceptable. The City Manager may review
the interview sheets of candidates marked not acceptable by a majority of the
interviewers. Unless the City Manager overrules the not acceptable
recommendations for just cause, no such candidate shall be recommended for
hire. A copy of the interview sheet is attached to Ordinance 174, 2022.
