GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 118.01 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   FIRE AND OTHER ALTERED GOODS SALE. A sale held out in such a manner as to
reasonably cause the public to believe that the sale will offer goods damaged
or altered by fire, smoke, water or other means.
   GOING-OUT-OF-BUSINESS SALE. A sale held out in such a manner as to
reasonably cause the public to believe that upon the disposal of the stock of
goods on hand the business will cease and be discontinued, including, but not
limited to, the following sales: adjuster’s, adjustment, alteration,
assignee’s, bankrupt, benefit of administrator’s, benefit of creditors’,
benefit of trustees, building coming down, closing, creditor’s committee,
creditor’s, end, executor’s, final days forced out, forced out of business
insolvents’, last days, lease expires, liquidation, loss of lease, mortgage
sale, receiver’s trustee’s, and quitting business.
   GOODS. Includes any goods, wares, merchandise or other property capable of
being the object of a sale regulated pursuant to this subchapter.
   REMOVAL OF BUSINESS SALE. A sale held out in such a manner as to reasonably
cause the public to believe that the person conducting the sale will cease and
discontinue business at the place of sale upon disposal of the stock of goods
on hand, and will then move to and resume business at a new location in the
city or will then continue business from other existing locations in the city.
(Prior Code, § 118.01) (Ord. 10-1961, passed 2-28-1961)
§ 118.02 REGULATIONS DEEMED SUPPLEMENTAL TO GENERAL LICENSING REGULATIONS.
   The provisions of this subchapter are intended to augment and be in addition
to the provisions of Chapters
112,
113,
115,
116 and
120. Where this subchapter imposes a greater restriction upon persons,
premises, businesses or practices than is imposed by Chapters
112,
113,
115,
116 and
120, this subchapter shall control.
(Prior Code, § 118.02) (Ord. 10-1961, passed 2-28-1961)
§ 118.03 LICENSE REQUIRED; EXEMPTIONS.
   (A)   A license issued by the Director of Finance of the city shall be
obtained by any person before selling or offering to sell any goods at a sale
to be advertised or held out by any means to be one of the following kinds:
      (1)   Going-out-of-business sale;
      (2)   Removal of business sale; or
      (3)   Fire and other altered stock sale.
   (B)   The provisions of this subchapter shall not apply to or affect the
following persons:
      (1)   Persons acting pursuant to an order or process of a court of
competent jurisdiction;
      (2)   Persons acting in accordance with their powers and duties as public
officials;
      (3)   Duly-licensed auctioneers, selling at auction;
      (4)   Persons conducting a sale of the type regulated pursuant to this
subchapter on the effective date, unless the sale is continued for a period of
more than 30 days from and after the effective date, in which event, the
person, at the lapse of the 30-day period, shall comply with the provisions of
this subchapter; or
      (5)   Any publisher of a newspaper, magazine or other publication, who
publishes in good faith, any advertisement, without knowledge of its false,
deceptive or misleading character, or without knowledge that the provisions of
this subchapter have not been complied with.
(Prior Code, § 118.03) (Ord. 10-1961, passed 2-28-1961) Penalty, see §
118.99
§ 118.04 LICENSE APPLICATION.
   A person desiring to conduct a sale regulated by this subchapter shall make
a written application to the Director of Finance setting forth and containing
the following information:
   (A)   The true name and address of the owner of the goods to be the object
of the sale;
   (B)   The true name and address of the person from whom he or she purchased
the goods to be sold and the price therefor, and if not purchased, the manner
of acquisition;
   (C)   A description of the place where the sale is to be held;
   (D)   The nature of the occupancy, whether by lease or sublease and the
effective date of termination of the occupancy;
   (E)   The dates of the period of time in which the sale is to be conducted;
   (F)   A full and complete statement of the facts in regard to the sale,
including the reason for the urgent and expeditious disposal of goods thereby
and the manner in which the sale will be conducted;
   (G)   The means to be employed in advertising the sale, together with the
proposed content of any advertisement; and
   (H)   A complete and detailed inventory of the goods to be sold at the sale
as disclosed by the applicant’s records. This inventory shall be attached to
and become part of the required application.
      (1)   All goods included in the inventory shall have been purchased by
the applicant for resale on bona fide orders without cancellation privileges,
and shall not comprise goods purchased on consignment.
      (2)   The inventory shall not include goods ordered in contemplation of
conducting a sale regulated pursuant to this subchapter. Any unusual purchase,
or additions to the stock of goods of the business hereby affected within 30
days before the filing of an application pursuant to this subchapter shall be
deemed to be of this character.
(Prior Code, § 118.04) (Ord. 10-1961, passed 2-28-1961) Penalty, see
118.99
§ 118.05 LICENSE FEE.
   Any applicant for a license pursuant to this subchapter shall submit to the
Director of Finance with his or her application a license fee of $50. Any
applicant for a renewal license pursuant to this subchapter shall submit to the
license officer with his or her renewal application a renewal license fee of
$50.
(Prior Code, § 118.05) (Ord. 10-1961, passed 2-28-1961)
§ 118.06 CONDITIONS FOR ISSUANCE.
   (A)   A license shall be issued as provided in this subchapter on the
following terms.
      (1)   Licensing period. The license shall authorize the sale described in
the application for a period of not more than 30 consecutive days, Sundays and
legal holidays excluded, following the issuance thereof. The Director of
Finance shall renew a license for one period of time only, this period to be in
addition to the 30 days permitted in the original license, and not to exceed 30
consecutive days, Sundays and holidays excluded, when he or she finds the
following.
         (a)   The facts exist justifying the license renewal.
         (b)   The licensee has filed an application for renewal.
         (c)   The licensee has submitted with the application for renewal a
revised inventory showing the items listed on the original inventory remaining
unsold, and not listing any goods not included in the original application and
inventory. For the purposes of this division (A)(1), any application for a
license under the provisions of this subchapter covering any goods previously
inventoried as required in this subchapter, shall be deemed to be an
application for renewal, whether presented by the original applicant, or by any
other person.
      (2)   Nature of sale. The license shall authorize only the one type of
sale described in the application at the location named therein.
      (3)   Saleable goods. The license shall authorize only the sale of goods
described in the inventory attached to the application.
      (4)   Surrender of general license. Upon being issued a license pursuant
to this subchapter for a going-out-of-business sale, the licensee shall
surrender to the Director of Finance all other business licenses he or she may
hold at that time applicable to the location and goods covered by the
application for a license under this subchapter, except business privilege
license.
      (5)   Transferability. Any license provided for in this subchapter shall
not be assignable or transferable.
   (B)   Any person who has not been the owner of a business advertised or
described in the application for a license provided for in this subchapter for
a period of at least six months prior to the date of the proposed sale shall
not be granted a license. However, upon the death of a person doing business in
this city his or her heirs, devisees or legatees shall have the right to apply
at any time for a license pursuant to this subchapter.
(Prior Code, § 118.06) (Ord. 10-1961, passed 2-28-1961)
§ 118.07 LICENSE APPLIES TO ONLY ONE PLACE OF BUSINESS.
   If a person applying for a license pursuant to this subchapter operates more
than one place of business, the license issued shall apply only to the one
store or branch specified in the application. No other store or branch shall
advertise or represent that it is cooperating with the licensed store, or in
any way participating in the licensed sale, nor shall the store or branch
conducting the licensed sale advertise or represent that any other store or
branch is cooperating with it or participating in any way in the licensed sale.
(Prior Code, § 118.07) (Ord. 10-1961, passed 2-28-1961) Penalty, see §
118.99
§ 118.08 INTERVAL BETWEEN SALES REQUIRED.
   Any person who has held a sale, as regulated by this subchapter, at the
location stated in the application, within one year last past from the date of
the application shall not be granted a license.
(Prior Code, § 118.08) (Ord. 10-1961, passed 2-28-1961)
§ 118.09 DUTIES OF LICENSEE.
   A licensee pursuant to this subchapter shall do the following:
   (A)   Adhere to inventory. Make no additions whatsoever, during the period
of the licensed sale, to the stock of goods set forth in the inventory attached
to the application for license;
   (B)   Advertise property. Refrain from employing any untrue, deceptive or
misleading advertising;
   (C)   Adhere to advertising. Conduct the licensed sale in strict conformity
with any advertising or holding out incident thereto;
   (D)   Keep duplicate inventory. Keep available at the place of sale a
duplicate copy of the inventory submitted with the application, and present the
duplicate to inspecting officials upon request; and
   (E)   Segregate noninventoried goods. Keep any other goods separate and
apart from the goods listed in the filed inventory as being objects of sale,
and make this distinction clear to the public by placing tags on all
inventoried goods in and about the place of sale apprising the public of the
status of all such goods.
(Prior Code, § 118.09) (Ord. 10-1961, passed 2-28-1961) Penalty, see §
118.99
GARAGE AND YARD SALES
§ 118.20 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CASUAL SALE. Includes, but is not limited to all sales entitled garage sale,
yard sale, attic sale, rummage sale, porch sale, moving sale or any similar
occasional casual sale of tangible personal property which is advertised by any
means or displayed in any manner whereby the public at large is or can be made
aware of the sale, except those sales provided for in §
118.23.
   GOODS. Generally includes any previously used goods, such as old clothes,
housewares and furniture normally used in a residence, or other similar
personal property capable of being the object of a sale regulated by this
subchapter.
   PERSON. Includes individuals, partnerships, voluntary associations and
corporations.
(Prior Code, § 118.20) (Ord. 68-1995, passed 6-5-1995)
§ 118.21 LICENSE REQUIRED; ISSUANCE.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to conduct a casual sale in the
city, without first filing the information specified and obtaining from the
City Cashier a license to do so, to be known as a CASUAL SALE LICENSE.
   (B)   The license shall be issued to any one person or for any one location
only two times within a 12-month period. No license shall be issued for more
than four consecutive calendar days for each sale. Each license issued under
this subchapter must be prominently displayed on the premises upon which the
sale is conducted, throughout the entire period of the licensed sale.
(Prior Code, § 118.21) (Ord. 68-1995, passed 6-5-1995) Penalty, see §
118.99
§ 118.22 INFORMATION TO BE FILED WITH CITY.
   The information required to be filed with the City Cashier pursuant to this
subchapter, shall be as follows:
   (A)   The name of the person, firm, group, corporation, association, or
organization conducting the sale;
   (B)   The name of the owner(s) of the property on which the sale is to be
conducted, and the consent of the owner if the applicant is other than the
owner;
   (C)   The location at which the sale is to be conducted;
   (D)   The number of days the sale is to be conducted;
   (E)   The date and nature of any past sale conducted;
   (F)   The relationship or connection the applicant may have had with any
other person, firm, group, or organization, association, or corporation
conducting any prior sale, and the date or dates of those sales;
   (G)   Whether or not the applicant has been issued any other vendors license
by any local, state or federal agency; and
   (H)   A sworn statement or affirmation by the person signing the application
for a license that the information therein given is full and true and known to
him or her to be so.
(Prior Code, § 118.22) (Ord. 68-1995, passed 6-5-1995) Penalty, see §
118.99
§ 118.23 EXEMPTIONS.
   (A)   The provisions of this subchapter shall not apply to or affect the
following persons or sales:
      (1)   Persons selling goods pursuant to an order or process of a court of
competent jurisdiction;
      (2)   Persons acting in accordance with their powers and duties as public
officials; and
      (3)   Any person selling or advertising for sale an item or items of
personal property which is specifically named or described in an advertisement
and which separate items do not exceed five in number.
   (B)   Upon tendering to the City Cashier the information required by §
118.22, and a determination by the City Cashier that the purpose of the casual
sale is to raise funds for an organization of a charitable or civic nature, the
City Cashier may suspend the permit and fees requirements contained in §
118.21 and may exempt the applicant from the frequency limitations contained in
§
118.21 and set the number of consecutive calendar days the casual sale shall be
authorized.
(Prior Code, § 118.23) (Ord. 68-1995, passed 6-5-1995)
FLEA MARKETS
§ 118.35 APPLICATION.
   Any individual, corporation, partnership or other entity which operates a
business, in what is commonly referred to as a flea market, in which table or
area space is rented or leased for the purpose of selling wares, goods or items
of any nature to the general public shall be covered by the provisions of this
subchapter. This subchapter is not intended to affect church or bazaar type
sales conducted by religious or non-profit organizations.
(Prior Code, § 118.35) (Ord. 93-1989, passed 9-5-1989; Ord. 30-1992, passed 4-
7-1992)
§ 118.36 RECORDS REQUIRED.
   The operator, owner or lessor of the flea market (hereafter operator) shall
maintain accurate records relating to the operation of the flea market in the
method and on forms established by the License Fee Administrator of the city
regarding vendors operating on space within the flea market. These records
shall include, but not be limited to, license receipts (as hereafter provided),
space rented, dates and times of operation, and sufficient identifying
information on the individual vendors and their suppliers. This information
shall be available to the License Fee Administrator at her request on the
premises of the flea market, and the operator shall be required to file a
monthly report with the License Fee Administrator on forms provided by the
city. The License Fee Administrator shall provide the operator with license
receipts (in triplicate) for issuance to the vendors as hereafter provided.
(Prior Code, § 118.36) (Ord. 30-1992, passed 4-7-1992)
§ 118.37 LICENSE REQUIRED; FEES.
   (A)   The individual vendor shall pay to the operator either $1 per day, $3
per week or $50 annually, at the vendor’s option, for the privilege of
operating the vendor’s business for any day during a calendar week the vendor
is in operation. The weekly payment made by the vendor shall be remitted by the
operator on a monthly basis to the city. The vendor shall provide to the city
or the operator whatever information is required by the city. Additionally, the
operator will provide the vendor with a license receipt which shall be posted
on a current basis at the vendor’s space at all times the vendor is in
operation in the city.
   (B)   In order to begin operation of the vendor’s business, a license
receipt must first be obtained from the operator.
   (C)   The operator shall be required to file with the city a yearly return
relating to vendors operating at a flea market. This return shall be in form
required by the city and shall be filed contemporaneously with the operator’s
business privilege return. It is understood nothing contained in this
subchapter exempts the operator from the provisions of
Chapter 115 of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 118.37) (Ord. 30-1992, passed 4-7-1992)
§ 118.38 VENDORS EXCLUDED FROM BUSINESS PRIVILEGE LICENSE REQUIREMENTS.
   Vendors in a flea market shall be excluded from the provisions of
Chapter 115 of this code of ordinances. The license fees contained in this
subchapter shall be the fee required of a vendor for the privilege of operating
a business within the city. The basis for this exclusion from the business
privilege license requirement is that a flea market vendor is by nature
transient and temporary, and primarily deals in used wares and goods.
(Prior Code, § 118.38) (Ord. 30-1992, passed 4-7-1992)
§ 118.39 ACTIVITIES NOT COVERED.
   It is understood that the provisions of this subchapter are not intended to
cover other activities which may be conducted in connection with the operation
of or on the premises of the flea market including, but not limited to,
auctions, truckload sales, etc. All of these activities shall continue to be
covered by the provisions of
Chapter 115 of this code of ordinances.
(Prior Code, § 118.39) (Ord. 30-1992, passed 4-7-1992)
§ 118.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person, association or corporation conducting any such sale
pursuant to §§
118.21 and
118.22 without being properly licensed therefor or who shall violate any of the
other terms and regulations of these sections, shall, upon conviction, be
guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to a fine or penalty not to exceed $500.
Each day the violation continues shall constitute a separate offense. It shall
be the responsibility of the Code Enforcement Division to enforce the licensing
requirements herein.
   (B)   Any person(s), firm(s) or corporation(s) violating the terms of §§
118.35 through
118.39 shall be deemed guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be fined in any sum
not less than $25 nor more than $100 in the discretion of the court or jury
trying the case. Each day in operation in violation constitutes a separate
offense.
   (C)   Any person, firm or corporation violating any other provisions of this
chapter shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be fined not more than $500
or imprisoned not more than 12 months, or both. Every day a violation continues
shall be deemed a separate offense and shall be punishable as such.
(Prior Code, § 118.99) (Ord. 30-1992, passed 4-7-1992; Ord. 68-1995, passed 6-
5-1995)

INSURANCE COMPANIES
§ 119.01 LICENSE FEE IMPOSED; EFFECTIVE DATE.
   There is imposed on each insurance company a license fee for the privilege
of engaging in the business of insurance within the corporate limits of the
city, effective July 1, 1999 and thereafter on a calendar year basis.
(Prior Code, § 120.25) (Ord. 21-1999, passed 3-18-1999)
§ 119.02 LICENSE FEE FOR COMPANIES WHICH ISSUE LIFE INSURANCE POLICIES.
   The license fee imposed upon each insurance company which issues life
insurance policies on the lives of persons residing within the corporate limits
of the city shall be 10% of the first year’s premiums actually collected within
each calendar quarter by reasons of the issuance of these policies.
(Prior Code, § 120.26) (Ord. 21-1999, passed 3-18-1999) Penalty, see §
119.99
§ 119.03 LICENSE FEE FOR COMPANIES WHICH ISSUE POLICIES OTHER THAN LIFE
INSURANCE.
   (A)   The license fee imposed upon each insurance company which issues any
insurance policy which is not a life insurance policy shall be 10% of the
premiums actually collected within each calendar quarter by reason of the
issuance of such policies on risks located within the corporate limits of the
city, on those classes of business which such company is authorized to
transact, less all premiums returned to policy holders.
   (B)   However, any license fee or tax imposed upon premium receipts shall
not include premiums received for insuring employers against liability for
personal injuries to their employees, or death caused thereby, under the
provisions of the Workers’ Compensation Act and shall not include premiums
received on policies of group health insurance provided for state employees
under KRS 18A.225(2) and 18A.228.
(Prior Code, § 120.27) (Ord. 21-1999, passed 3-18-1999) Penalty, see §
119.99
§ 119.04 DUE DATE; INTEREST CHARGED ON LATE PAYMENTS.
   All license fees imposed by this subchapter shall be due no later than 30
days after the end of each calendar quarter. License fees which are not paid on
or before the due date shall bear interest at the tax interest rate as defined
in KRS 131.010(6).
(Prior Code, § 120.28) (Ord. 21-1999, passed 3-18-1999) Penalty, see §
119.99
§ 119.05 BREAKDOWN OF COLLECTIONS TO BE FURNISHED TO CITY.
   Every insurance company subject to the license fee imposed by this
subchapter shall annually, by March 31, furnish the city with a written
breakdown of all collections in the preceding calendar year for the following
categories of insurance:
   (A)   Casualty;
   (B)   Automobile;
   (C)   Inland marine;
   (D)   Fire and allied perils;
   (E)   Health;
   (F)   Professional malpractice;
   (G)   Bonds;
   (H)   Life; and
   (I)   All others.
(Prior Code, § 120.29) (Ord. 21-1999, passed 3-18-1999) Penalty, see §
119.99

93.01 and

ELECTRICAL CONTRACTORS
§ 119.35 PURPOSE.
   This subchapter is hereby declared to be remedial and shall be construed to
secure the beneficial interests and purposes of public safety, health and
welfare, through structural strength and stability, and safety of life and
property from fire hazards incidental to installation, alteration, repair and/
or removal of the electrical wiring or equipment.
(Prior Code, § 120.65) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993) Penalty, see §
119.99
§ 119.36 COMPLIANCE REQUIRED; STATE CODE ADOPTED BY REFERENCE.
   All electrical wiring in installation of electrical apparatus and appliances
for furnishing light, heat or power in the city shall comply in all respects
with the rules and regulations of the National Electrical Code which is
incorporated into the State Standards of Safety and which is hereby adopted as
the minimum standard in the city.
(Prior Code, § 120.66) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993) Penalty, see §
119.99
§ 119.37 ELECTRICAL CONTRACTOR DEFINED.
   ELECTRICAL CONTRACTOR means any person, other than as stated in §
119.43, who holds a valid contractor’s license issued by the city, and who
proceeds with or employs others for the construction, alteration, repairs or
additions to any electrical wiring used for the purpose of furnishing heat,
light or power within the city. The provisions in this subchapter shall in no
manner be construed to prevent an individual who is the owner and occupant of
an existing single-family residence to observe the privileges of this
subchapter, relating to electrical wiring, from installing, altering or
repairing, by and for himself or herself electrical wiring on his or her
single-family dwelling, as long as required permits are obtained and the work
passes a rough-in and final inspection.
(Prior Code, § 120.67) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993)
§ 119.38 ELECTRICAL CONTRACTOR’S LICENSE REQUIRED.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to engage in the business of installing,
altering or repairing, within the city, any electrical wiring, devices or
equipment unless such individual is the holder of an electrical contractor’s
license.
(Prior Code, § 120.68) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993)
§ 119.39 OBTAINING AND REVIEWING LICENSE.
   (A)   Those persons desiring to become electrical contractors in the city
must first pass the state approved test for electrical contractor administered
by the National Assessment Institute.
   (B)   Satisfactory completion of the electrical contractor examination
requirement contained in KRS 227.490, upon application and payment of the
requisite fees, is required to obtain an electrical contractor certificate
issued by the Kentucky Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction.
   (C)   Any person who holds a valid electrical contractor license issued by
the city prior to the effective date of Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993, may,
within 30 days of the expiration of the license, renew the license without
taking an examination.
   (D)   Electrical contractors whose license has expired for over one year
shall be required to be re-examined before renewing their license.
(Prior Code, § 120.69) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993)
§ 119.40 INSURANCE REQUIRED OF CONTRACTORS.
   (A)   All electrical contractors shall maintain premises and products and
completed operation liability insurance coverage in the amount of not less than
$250,000 and shall show and place on file with the Division of Code Enforcement
proof of same prior to being issued a contractor’s license at the beginning of
each year.
   (B)   The required liability insurance shall be kept current during the
licensing period and shall include coverage for those employed by the
contractor.
   (C)   Failure to comply with division (A) of this section shall result in
the license being void.
   (D)   Proof of license and insurance shall be on the person of an electrical
contractor.
   (E)   The city requests that the insurer notify the Division of Code
Enforcement 30 days in advance of any cancellation of the policy.
(Prior Code, § 120.70) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993)
§ 119.41 PERMIT FOR INSTALLATION, ALTERATION REQUIRED.
   (A)   Electrical wiring or equipment shall not be installed nor shall any
alteration be made in any existing installation without first obtaining a
permit from the Division of Code Enforcement, the fee for which shall be $10.
The application and issuance of said permit is governed by all applicable
sections of the Kentucky Building Code, including, but not limited to, Article
27, and by the rules and regulations established by the Division of Code
Enforcement.
   (B)   A permit shall not be required for the execution and uses of the
classes of work specified in §§ 2704.2.1 through 2704.2.4 of the Kentucky
Building Code.
   (C)   Electrical permit forms shall be provided by the Division of Code
Enforcement.
   (D)   The Division of Code Enforcement shall issue permits, approve licenses
in accordance with this subchapter, maintain records, promulgate rules and
regulations, and conduct on-site inspections to ensure compliance with this
subchapter.
   (E)   All electrical wiring, apparatus and appliances hereafter installed in
the city shall be inspected by a state certified electrical inspector, and it
shall be unlawful to use any new electrical installation in any building,
structure or premises before same has been inspected and approved as required
by §§ 2700.5 and 2704.1 of the Kentucky Building Code.
   (F)   The electrical inspector shall check for permits and notify the
Division of Code Enforcement of permit violations. Inspection stickers and
certificates of compliance shall be provided at the job site by the inspector.
   (G)   All inspection fees shall be paid to the Inspector by the customer.
(Prior Code, § 120.71) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993)
§ 119.42 AUTHORITY TO TURN OFF CURRENT OR DISCONNECT WIRES IN EMERGENCIES.
   The Chief of the Fire Department or his or her designated representatives
shall have the authority to cause the turning off of all electrical currents
and to cut or disconnect, in cases of emergency, any wires where such
electrical currents are dangerous to life and property or where such wires may
interfere with the work or progress of the Fire Department in fighting fires.
(Prior Code, § 120.72) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993)
§ 119.43 EXCEPTIONS TO TESTING AND LICENSING REQUIREMENTS.
   (A)   Public utility companies and corporations engaged in the manufacture
or distribution of electrical energy for commercial purposes, or their
employees, shall not be required to obtain licenses for the manufacture,
transmission, distribution and metering of electrical energy, and all repairs
and maintenance connected therewith, telephone, telegraph and other related
companies shall not be required to obtain licenses to engage in these
activities. Full-time employees of a manufacturing facility, with 10,000 or
more square feet at the site, shall not be required to obtain licenses to
engage in electrical maintenance. Individuals engaged in the installation and/
or repair of specialized equipment may connect to the on-site disconnect
without first obtaining a license. Specialized equipment shall include water
heaters, air conditioners, furnaces, elevators, electrical appliances and
related equipment. This is not to be construed as permitting these individuals
to make any electrical connections or do any electrical wiring other than what
is necessary to connect to the on-site disconnect or to repair the equipment
itself.
   (B)   Any electrical contractor who has been lawfully engaged in the active
practice of his or her profession for five of the six years next preceding his
or her application in a jurisdiction outside the city, and can satisfactorily
document this experience, may be issued a license to practice in the city
without further examination provided that the qualifications, which must
include passing an examination required to be licensed in such other
jurisdiction, are equal to or higher than those of the National Assessment
Institute. An examination may still be required, however, in such instances
where there is reasonable doubt as to the nature or quality of the applicant’s
work or the standards of said other jurisdiction.
(Prior Code, § 120.73) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993)
§ 119.44 APPEALS BOARD OF ELECTRICIANS.
   There is hereby created a Board to be known as the Appeals Board of
Electricians. The Board shall be composed of three members appointed by the
Mayor and approved by the Board of City Commissioners, each of whom shall be
knowledgeable in the electrical field. The Appeals Board shall consist of one
city Fire Department official, one electrical contractor, and one electrical
engineer or architect. Terms shall be for four years provided that the initial
term of one member shall be two years to provide for staggered terms. Vacancies
shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment, and the
successor shall be appointed for the unexpired term. Any member may be
appointment for additional terms.
(Prior Code, § 120.74) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993)
§ 119.45 LIABILITY FOR DAMAGE CAUSED.
   This subchapter shall not be construed to relieve from loss or lessen the
responsibility or liability of any party owning, operating, controlling or
installing any electrical wiring, devices or equipment for damage to person or
property caused by any defect therein; nor shall the Division of Code
Enforcement be held as assuming any such liability by reason of the inspections
authorized herein or permits of approval issued as herein provided.
(Prior Code, § 120.75) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993)
FOOD SERVICES
§ 119.60 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   FOOD SERVICE. Includes an business, including temporary and mobile food
operations, or any other entity engaged in the handling of raw meat and raw
vegetables, the preparation of and the service for consumption of food by the
public, e.g., restaurants, grocery meat and produce departments, school and
hospital cafeterias, caterers, banquet facilities, nursing home kitchens and
other similar businesses/enterprises.
(Prior Code, § 120.85) (Ord. 95-2018, passed 6-25-2018)
§ 119.61 REQUIRED HEPATITIS A VACCINATION.
   (A)   The Board of City Commissioners requires that those workers engaged in
food service responsibilities in businesses and other entities located within
the city shall be required to have a hepatitis A vaccination, including
appropriate boosters (which should be administered six months after the first
dose), in order to perform such duties. Newly hired or engaged food service
workers must receive the first hepatitis A vaccine at least two weeks prior to
their handling of food for public consumption. This requirement shall go into
effect on July 1, 2018 and each business/entity shall have four weeks from that
date to complete the inoculations of such workers recognizing that it takes a
minimum of two weeks for an individual to begin building immunity.
   (B)   A food service worker who has been previously inoculated with
appropriate boosters with proof of such inoculation shall not be required to
undergo additional inoculation upon providing satisfactory proof of same.
   (C)   All businesses and other entities shall be required to maintain
records of the inoculation of their affected workers during the course of such
workers’ engagement in providing food services. Such proof of inoculation shall
be made available to city inspectors or County Public Health inspectors upon
request.
   (D)   Failure to maintain such records or provide such proof when requested
as provided by this subchapter as well as noncompliance with any other
provision of this subchapter, shall be considered as violations of the
subchapter.
   (E)   The requirements of this section shall not apply to women who are
pregnant, no to those individuals who in the written opinion of his or her duly
licensed attending physician that such inoculation would be injurious to the
person’s health, nor to those persons who are opposed to vaccination on
religious grounds and sign a written sworn statement to that effect.
(Prior Code, § 120.86) (Ord. 95-2018, passed 6-25-2018) Penalty, see §
119.99
§ 119.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   Any person who violates any provision of this chapter, for which
another penalty is not provided, shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be
fined not more than $500 or imprisoned not more than 12 months, or both. Each
day a violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense and shall be
punishable as such.
   (B)   Any person, firm or corporation who violates any provisions of §§
119.35 through
119.45 shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be fined not less than $10
nor more than $100, or imprisoned not more than 50 days, or both. Each day any
violation continues shall be deemed a separate offense.
   (C)   Any person, business or entity who violates any of the provisions of
§§
119.60 and
119.61 shall, upon conviction, be fined not less than $50 nor more than any
stated amount provided in KRS 534.040(2)(c). Each day of violation after
notification shall constitute a separate offense.
(Prior Code, § 120.99) (Ord. 97-1993, passed 9-2-1993; Ord. 95-2018, passed 6-
25-2018; Ord. 112, 2019, passed 8-8-2019)

SOLICITING DOOR-TO-DOOR
§ 120.01 REGISTRATION; CERTAIN INFORMATION REQUIRED; TEMPORARY SOLICITATION.
   (A)   Any person, group, organization, business or corporation, profit or
non-profit, that intends to engage in door-to-door within the city shall be
required to register with the designated party at the Police Department on
forms created for that purpose by the designee of the City Manager providing
identifying information, including times and dates of proposed activity,
parties that will be participating, locations of the activity, purpose of the
solicitation and other information reasonably required to regulate the
activity.
   (B)   Any person, organization, group, business, or corporation, profit or
non-profit, intending to engage in solicitation on a temporary basis shall be
required to purchase a city business license notifying the Occupational
License/Net Profit Division of the Finance Department of the type of
solicitation along with the name of each individual participating in the door
to door solicitation. Any such solicitation shall be conducted only during
daylight hours, but no later than 8:00 p.m.
(Prior Code, § 121.01) (Ord. 136-1983, passed 10-6-1983; Ord. 78-2010, passed
8-5-2010) Penalty, see §
120.99
§ 120.02 CITY NOT LIABLE.
   The applicant shall execute a release and shall hold the city harmless from
any and all damages, injuries, and claims as a result of any solicitation
activities.
(Prior Code, § 121.02) (Ord. 136-1983, passed 10-6-1983; Ord. 78-2010, passed
8-5-2010)
SOLICITING OTHER THAN BY DOOR-TO-DOOR
§ 120.15 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   PUBLIC PLACE. A publicly owned building and premises appurtenant thereto,
any public park, sidewalk, median or other right-of-way open to the general
public and includes alleys, bridges, buildings, driveways, parking lots, parks,
plazas, skywalks and streets.
   SOLICIT and SOLICITATION.
      (1)   To make any request in person while in a public place, for an
immediate grant of money, goods or any other form of gratuity from another
person(s) when the person making the request is not known to the person(s) who
are the subject of the request.
      (2)   However, the terms SOLICIT and SOLICITATION shall not mean the act
of passively standing or sitting with a sign or other indicator that a donation
of money, goods or any other form of gratuity is being sought without any vocal
request other than a response to an inquiry by another person.
(Prior Code, § 121.15) (Ord. 113-2015, passed 12-10-2015; Ord. 114-2016, passed
10-13-2016)
§ 120.16 PROHIBITIONS.
   It is unlawful for any person to solicit in the following places or under
the following conditions:
   (A)   In any public transportation vehicle;
   (B)   Within 20 feet of an automatic teller machine or public entrance to a
business;
   (C)   From any operator or occupant of a motor vehicle or from any person
entering or exiting a motor vehicle;
   (D)   On private property without permission from the owner;
   (E)   From any person engaged in the act of placing money in a parking meter
or from any person engaged in the act of locating money on his or her person or
within his or her personal belongings for any activity including a purchase or
donation;
   (F)   Within any private parking garages or private parking lots;
   (G)   At any bus stop;
   (H)   Within 20 feet of any crosswalk;
   (I)   While standing in line waiting to be admitted to a commercial
establishment;
   (J)   Within any outdoor dining area; or
   (K)   Within any median or in a street.
(Prior Code, § 121.16) (Ord. 113-2015, passed 12-10-2015; Ord. 114-2016, passed
10-13-2016) Penalty, see §
120.99
§ 120.17 SOLICITING IN AN AGGRESSIVE MANNER.
   It is unlawful for any person to solicit in an aggressive manner. AGGRESSIVE
MANNER is defined as:
   (A)   Soliciting in a manner that impedes access to or from, or use of a
building, vehicle or establishment;
   (B)   Soliciting in a manner that would alarm, intimidate, threaten, menace,
harass, or coerce a reasonable person;
   (C)   By following behind, ahead or alongside, blocking the path of, or
continuing to solicit a person who walks or drives away from the person
soliciting or who gives notice or demonstrates verbally or physically that such
solicitation is offensive, unwelcome or that the solicitation should cease;
   (D)   By using profane or abusive language or gestures either during the
solicitation or following a refusal, or making any statement, gesture or other
communication that would cause a reasonable person to be fearful or would be
perceived as a threat; or
   (E)   By touching the solicited person without a statement, gesture or other
communication that the person being solicited consents to the touching.
(Prior Code, § 121.17) (Ord. 113-2015, passed 12-10-2015) Penalty, see §
120.99
§ 120.18 FALSE OR MISLEADING REPRESENTATIONS.
   It is unlawful for any person to knowingly make a false or misleading
representation in the course of soliciting a donation. False or misleading
representations include, but are not limited to the following:
   (A)   Stating that the donation is needed to meet a specific need, when the
person soliciting already has sufficient funds to meet that need and does not
disclose that fact;
   (B)   Stating that the donation is needed to meet a need that does not
exist;
   (C)   Stating that the person soliciting is from out of town and stranded,
or that he or she is homeless when that representation is not true;
   (D)   Stating or representing that the person soliciting is a member of a
military service when the person soliciting is neither a present nor a former
member of a military service; and
   (E)   Stating or representing that the person soliciting suffers from a
mental or physical disability or deformity when the person soliciting does not
suffer the disability or deformity indicated.
(Prior Code, § 121.18) (Ord. 113-2015, passed 12-10-2015) Penalty, see §
120.99
§ 120.99 PENALTY.
   (A)   The violation of any provision of this chapter shall be punishable by
fine not to exceed the amount permitted under KRS 534.040 for violations per
solicitor and each day of violation shall constitute a separate offense.
   (B)   A violation of §
120.16 shall be punishable consistent with KRS 534.040(2)(c). A violation of §§
120.17 or
120.18 shall be punishable consistent with KRS 534.040(2)(a).
(Prior Code, § 121.99) (Ord. 78-2010, passed 8-5-2010; Ord. 113-2015, passed
12-10-2015)

WEAPONS
§ 130.15 DISCHARGE IN CITY PROHIBITED; EXCEPTIONS.
   (A)   It shall be lawful and permissible for the following persons under the
following conditions to discharge firearms within the corporate limits of the
city:
      (1)   Peace officers, properly supervised, in practice on an established
practice range;
      (2)   The National Guard, in practice, at the armory or on an established
practice range, properly supervised;
      (3)   Any organized gun club or group properly supervised, engaged in
skeet or trap shooting at a place established for that purpose; and
      (4)   The City of Ashland certified animal control officer in the course
of required duties.
   (B)   All such activities as described and designated above shall be carried
on at a place and in such a manner so as not to constitute a menace to the
public safety or tranquility.
   (C)   Violation of this section shall be deemed a misdemeanor and punishable
pursuant to KRS 534.040.
(Prior Code, § 130.15) (Ord. 8-1967, passed 3-13-1967; Ord. 100, passed 7-21-
1994; Ord. 81, 2020, passed 6-18-2020) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 130.16 TOY GUNS, AIR GUNS, BB GUNS AND THE LIKE.
   (A)   No person shall fire or discharge an air rifle, BB gun or other
instrument capable of issuing a projectable, whether by air, gas, spray or
other means, while on any public street, public sidewalk, or in any public
place, nor shall any person fire or discharge such rifle, gun or other
instrument described herein into or across any public street, public sidewalk
or public place. It shall be unlawful for a parent or guardian of a minor to
knowingly permit a minor to violate this section.
   (B)   It shall be lawful and permissible to fire or discharge within the
corporate limits of the city only on private property, with the permission of
the property owner, any air rifle, BB gun or other toy gun.
   (C)   (1)   It shall be lawful and permissible for the following persons
under the following conditions to discharge any type of toy guns within the
corporate limits of the city:
         (a)   Peace officers, properly supervised, in practice on an
established practice range;
         (b)   The National Guard, in practice, at the armory or on an
established practice range, properly supervised;
         (c)   Any organized gun club or group properly supervised, engaged in
skeet or trap shooting at a place established for that purpose;
         (d)   Any organized club or group properly supervised upon approval by
the Ashland Board of City Commissioners may discharge between the hours of 12:
00 noon and 10:00 p.m. any smoothbore BB gun with metallic sights in which the
propelling force is developed through the use of a compressed spring, gas or
compressed air, at a fully enclosed shooting range, provided that supervision
is available for each participant by a certified gun instructor. No BB guns
that have been altered from factory manufacture are permitted. The range shall
be fully enclose and not permit discharge of BBs or pellets outside of its
perimeter. Sight and hearing protection must be provided for participants. Any
organization seeking such approval must provide liability insurance with the
city named as an insured in the sum of not less than $1,000,000 for the dates
of the application. The organization shall also sign an indemnity agreement
with the city holding the city and its employees harmless from any injury that
might arise from the use of the shooting range; and
         (e)   The city’s certified Animal Control Officer in the course of
required duties.
      (2)   All such activities as described and designated above shall be
carried on at a place and in such a manner so as not to constitute a menace to
the public safety or tranquility.
   (D)   It shall be permissible to discharge any spring controlled device with
a foam based projectable in public places provided no intent to injure or
damage property is involved.
   (E)   It shall be impermissible to paint, color or otherwise modify a
commercially available toy gun to make it appear as a real gun, or use a
painted, colored or otherwise modified commercially manufactured toy gun that
appears as a real gun.
   (F)   Violation of this section shall be deemed a misdemeanor and punishable
pursuant to KRS 534.040.
(Prior Code, § 130.16) (Ord. 107-2015, passed 11-12-2015; Ord. 80, 2020, passed
6-18-2020) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 130.17 CARRYING OR POSSESSION OF SPECIFIC ITEMS IN ASHLAND CITY BUILDING.
   (A)   No person, including any employee of the city, except sworn officers
of the Ashland Police Department or other law enforcement officers, shall have
in his or her possession or on his or her person within the confines of the
Ashland City Building located at 1700 Greenup Avenue and/or the Ashland Police
Station located at 201 17th Street, Ashland, Kentucky, any of the following:
      (1)   Concealed deadly weapon;
      (2)   Any knife, except an ordinary pocketknife with a blade less than
two inches in length that folds into the handle, doesn’t open by pressing a
button and doesn’t lock into place, or other knife routinely used in the
performance of city duties;
      (3)   Billy, nightstick or club;
      (4)   Blackjack or slapjack;
      (5)   Nunchaku karate sticks;
      (6)   Shuriken or death star;
      (7)   Artificial knuckles made from metal, plastic or other similar hard
material;
      (8)   Sharp objects such as scissors, screwdrivers, ice picks for
example;
      (9)   Flammable liquids or gasses; or
      (10)   Any other item that the city’s Police Department determines could
be utilized as a weapon.
   (B)   As a condition of entry to the aforereferenced buildings, all persons
entering are required to consent to passing through a security checkpoint for
prohibited items including the use of a security wand or pat-down when metal is
indicated or for those medically unable to pass through a metal detector.
   (C)   Violation of this section may result in denial of entry to the
building or portion of the building, or an order to leave the building or
portion of the building, or, if an employee of the city, disciplinary measures
up to and including dismissal from employment, unless the City Manager granted
prior consent to the city employee to possess such item on city property.
(Prior Code, § 130.17) (Ord. 126, 2019, passed 9-12-2019)
§ 130.18 CARRYING CONCEALED DEADLY WEAPONS.
   (A)   No person, including employees of the city shall carry a concealed
deadly weapon into or on any building or portion of a building owned leased or
controlled by the city, except as otherwise provided in this section.
   (B)   Exemptions mandated by state law.
      (1)   This section shall not apply to buildings or portions of buildings
owned, leased or controlled by the city which are used for public housing by
private persons, firing ranges and private dwellings.
      (2)   This section shall not apply to sworn officers of the Police
Department and other law enforcement officers authorized to carry concealed
deadly weapons pursuant to KRS 527.020.
   (C)   The Director of Public Services shall post signs at the entrances of
all city owned, leased or controlled buildings or portion of buildings which
shall read as follows:
CARRYING OF CONCEALED DEADLY WEAPONS ON THESE PREMISES IS PROHIBITED BY ORD.
88, 1996 OF THE CITY OF ASHLAND.
   (D)   Violation of this section may result in denial of entry to the
building or portion of the building, or an order to leave the building or
portion of the building, or, if an employee of the city, disciplinary measures
up to and including dismissal from employment.
   (E)   Nothing in this section shall be construed as permitting the carrying
of a concealed deadly weapon in violation of KRS 527.020.
(Prior Code, § 130.18) (Ord. 88-1996, passed 8-15-1996)

§ 131.01 TRESPASSING, BURNING TRASH ON FLOOD WALL.
   It shall be unlawful for any person to trespass upon the Ashland flood wall
or any portion of the permanent right-of-way thereof, to burn trash within 25
feet of such wall, to post bills upon such wall or such right-of-way, to erect
any building or fence on such right-of-way or to deposit any material, rubbish
or equipment thereon.
(Prior Code, § 131.02) (Ord. 19-1950, passed - -1950) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 131.02 REGULATIONS FOR USE OF SHOPPING CARTS.
   (A)   Definitions.   For the purpose of this section, the following
definitions shall apply unless the context clearly indicates or requires a
different meaning.
      CART. Any rolling or non-rolling basket or container commonly used in so-
called supermarkets or self-service stores.
      STORE. Includes any individual store, chain-store and/or supermarket.
   (B)   Unlawful acts.
      (1)   It shall be unlawful for any person to take or use without
authority any cart from the premises of any store. Premises includes adjacent,
paved parking area.
      (2)   It shall be unlawful for any person to abandon or suffer to be
abandoned any cart, from any store or supermarket, on any street, highway,
alley, boulevard or public place within the city.
      (3)   It shall be unlawful for any person to provide carts for patrons’
use on the store premises, unless such carts bear permanent markings denoting
the owner.
   (C)   Abandoned carts. Whenever any cart is found abandoned on any street,
highway, boulevard, alley or other place open to the public, the owner of such
cart shall be notified of its location. If the cart is not retrieved by the
owner within two hours of notification, the Police Department shall impound the
property and shall again notify the owner of the impoundment. The Department of
Public Services shall be responsible for picking up impounded carts and
transporting them for storage in the Police Department Property Room. After the
second notification, the owner of the cart shall have a period of 24 hours in
which he or she may reclaim the cart by paying a pickup and storage fee of $5
at the Police Department, between the hours of 8:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m.,
excluding weekends and holidays when there is not a property officer on duty.
Failure to reclaim the carts as provided after the second notification shall be
unlawful and shall be a violation of this section. The notices provided for
herein shall only be given to the person in charge of the store which owns the
cart.
   (D)   Failure to claim. If any owner shall fail to claim the carts or if the
cart owner is not identified or properly marked, the city may dispose of same
within 30 days after impoundment.
   (E)   Post ordinance. Any store using shopping carts as defined in this
section shall post a copy of Ord. 64-1988 upon the premises in a place where
the same can be readily seen by the public.
(Prior Code, § 131.03) (Ord. 64-1988, passed 7-19-1988) Penalty, see §
10.99

Section

Statutory reference:
   Oil, gas, and salt water wells, see KRS Chapter 353
§ 150.01 DRILLING PERMIT REQUIRED; FEE AND BOND.
   (A)   Each person desiring to drill or explore for gas or oil at any point
within the city shall apply to the Director of Public Services for a permit,
submitting with the application for the permit a map showing the exact location
of the well proposed to be drilled and also the highways to be traversed in
bringing in the boilers, drills and other equipment necessary to drill the
well. After the Director of Public Services is satisfied with the location of
the well in question and that it will not unduly interfere with the safety of
the persons and property, he or she shall issue a permit on payment of the sum
of $25 for each well drilled and on the giving a bond, with corporate surety,
in the amount of $10,000 conditioned as follows: that the city shall be
indemnified from all damages caused by the applicant in the moving of boilers,
rigs or other equipment used in the drilling of the well over the streets of
the city and further conditioned to pay all damages that may be occasioned to
any person or property by reason of the drilling of the well or by the shooting
of the well.
   (B)   The $25 collected for each permit shall be paid into the city treasury
and shall be used for general purposes.
(Prior Code, § 150.01) Penalty, see §
10.99
§ 150.02 PROTECTION OF FRESH WATER SUPPLY.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person to drill a well in the city for
oil, gas or other purposes unless provision is made to protect the ground
supply of fresh water above a datum plane located 240 feet above sea level. All
wells drilled below the datum plane of 240 feet above sea level shall be cased
off so that no salt water can enter the strata containing fresh water. This
protection shall be a continued obligation on the part of the owner of the land
on which a well is drilled or the lessee of the land, and shall continue during
the operation of the well.
   (B)   In the event the well is abandoned, it shall be plugged according to
provisions of state law and the plugs shall be installed below the 240 feet
datum plane to ensure permanent protection to the fresh water. In case of a dry
well, a proper and sufficient plug shall be installed in the well at the datum
plane, so that no salt water shall enter the fresh water strata.
(Prior Code, § 150.02) Penalty, see §
10.99
Statutory reference:
   Plugging gas or oil wells, see KRS 353.110 through 353.180
§ 150.03 REPORT OF COMPLETION OF DRILLING; INSPECTION.
   On the completion of drilling a well within the city, the owner or lessee of
the well shall report completion to the Department of Public Services. A
representative of the Department of Public Services shall examine the well, and
shall report to the Director of Public Services that the casing and plugging is
properly installed, and that all work in connection with the drilling of the
well and casing and plugging has been fully done and completed according to the
provisions of §
153.02. The report shall be left or filed with the Director of Public Services,
who is hereby appointed custodian of such reports.
(Prior Code, § 150.03)

GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 151.01 ADOPTION OF CERTAIN STATE AND NATIONAL CODES.
   (A)   The 2018 Kentucky Building Code and the 2018 Kentucky Residential Code
as promulgated and/or approved by the Commonwealth’s Board of Housing,
Buildings and Construction, and as they may be revised or amended, are hereby
adopted in full as an ordinance of the City of Ashland, Boyd County, Kentucky,
by reference, as if set out at length herein.
   (B)   Copies of the above codes, together with copies of all regulations or
pamphlets adopted or referred to thereunder, shall be kept on file in the
office of Code Enforcement of the city. Such Codes shall be made available for
reference at all times during the regular office hours of such officials.
   (C)   An attested copy of the ordinance adopting this section shall be
transmitted to the Department of Housing, Buildings and Construction of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky.
   (D)   The Department of Planning and Community Development, Division of Code
Enforcement, shall be the designated local enforcement agency for the above
codes.

§ 151.02 ADOPTION OF STANDARDS OF SAFETY; NATIONAL FIRE CODE.
   (A)   The Kentucky Standards of Safety (Fire Prevention Code) as promulgated
in 815 KAR 10:060 by the Commissioner of the Department of Housing, Building
and Construction on the advice and recommendation of the State Fire Marshal, is
hereby adopted by reference as if set out in full. A copy shall be kept in the
office of the Fire Chief at all times.
   (B)   The National Fire Code and all codes a part thereof, as promulgated by
the National Fire Protection Association, Batterymarch Park, Quincy,
Massachusetts 02269, a copy of which is on file in the office of the Fire Chief
of the City of Ashland, is hereby adopted in full by reference, as if set out
in full. A copy shall be kept in the office of the Fire Chief. The Fire Chief
shall at all times keep in his or her possession for reference a copy of the
Uniform Fire Code and/or any future codes adopted by the NFPA.
   (C)   The Ashland Fire Department shall be designated as the local
enforcement agency for the Standards of Safety and National Fire Code as
appointed by the Board of City Commissioners.
   (D)   All final decisions of the fire code official of the city shall be
appealable to a local appeals board pursuant to the procedures adopted by the
Board of City Commissioners.
(Prior Code, § 151.02) (Ord. 101-1999, passed 8-19-1999; Ord. 66-2007, passed

§ 151.03 ENCROACHMENTS ON PUBLIC PROPERTY PROHIBITED; REMOVAL.
   (A)   It shall be unlawful for any person, other than the city, to construct
or maintain any building or other structure, or portion thereof, or
appurtenance thereto, except sidewalks, walkways, steps or driveways used as a
means of approach, ingress and egress to and from privately owned real estate,
on the publicly owned, or city property, within the city. Any sidewalks,
walkways, steps and driveways, above mentioned, shall be privately constructed
only after obtaining a permit so to do, issued and obtained from the office of
the Building Inspector of the city as other building permits are issued and
obtained.
   (B)   All privately owned structures prohibited by division (A) of this
section or portions thereof, not included within the exceptions set out in
division (A) of this section now standing or encroaching on public property
shall be removed therefrom within 30 days after written notice to remove them
issued by the office of the City Manager.
   (C)   In the case of the failure or refusal of any person to remove any of
the structures prohibited by divisions (A) and (B) of this section within the
limit of time fixed by the notice provided for in division (B) of this section,
the city shall have the right to remove the structures at the cost of the
abutting property owner or the owner of the land on which the structure is
located.
(Prior Code, § 151.03) (Ord. 20-1954, passed 9-24-1954) Penalty, see §
151.99

any building or structure, including accessory buildings, or to commence the
moving, alteration or demolition of any building or structure, including
accessory buildings, until the Building Inspector has issued a permit for the
work.

lines and to street or road lines of all buildings or structures to be erected,
altered, moved or demolished and of any building or structure already on the
lot.
   (B)   For all building permits, the applicant shall furnish two sets of
detailed plans as follows. Plans for parking spaces and driveways are to be
included as required by the city zoning ordinance.
   (C)   The applicant shall also state the existing and intended use of all
such buildings and supply other information as may be required by the Building
Inspector to ensure that the provisions of this subchapter, the city zoning
ordinance and other pertinent ordinances or laws, are being observed. All
applications, sketches and other information supplied in order to obtain a
building permit must be signed by the applicant.

§ 151.20 ISSUANCE.

as set forth in the application, is in conformity with the provisions of this
subchapter, the city zoning ordinance, and other ordinances or laws then in
force, the Building Inspector shall issue a permit for the excavation,
construction, alteration, moving or demolition within 14 days of the filing of

approvals issued by the city or other governmental units, departments or

§ 151.21 REFUSAL.
   (A)   If the application for a permit and the drawings filed therewith
describe work which does not conform to the requirements of this subchapter or
other pertinent laws or ordinances, the Building Inspector shall not issue a
permit, but shall return the drawings to the applicant with his or her refusal
to issue the permit.
   (B)   When a permit is refused, the Building Inspector shall state the
refusal in writing, setting forth in detail all reasons for refusal and shall,
within seven working days, mail notice of the refusal to the applicant at the
address indicated in the application.

   When application for permit to erect or enlarge a building has been filed
and pending issuance of the permits, the Building Inspector may, at his or her

holder of such a special permit shall proceed at his or her own risk and

§ 151.24 PERMIT IS LICENSE.
   (A)   A permit issued shall be construed to be a license to proceed with the
work and shall not be construed as authority to violate, cancel, alter or set
aside any of the provisions of this chapter, the zoning ordinance or other
pertinent ordinances or laws. Such issuance shall not prevent the Building
Inspector from thereafter requiring a correction of errors in plans or in
construction, or of violations of this subchapter.
   (B)   Any permit issued shall become invalid if the authorized work is not
commenced within one year after issuance of the permit, or if the authorized
work is suspended or abandoned for a period of six months after the time of
commencing the work. For reasonable cause, the Building Inspector may grant one
or more extensions of time for additional periods not exceeding 90 days each.
   (C)   Any demolition or moving permit issued shall become invalid unless the
work authorized by it shall have been completed within 90 days after its
issuance.
(Prior Code, § 151.24) (Ord. 30-1974, passed 8-20-1974; Ord. 73-2008, passed 6-
23-2008)
§ 151.25 DRAWINGS TO BE KEPT AT SITE.
   When the Building Inspector issues a permit, he or she shall endorse two
sets of plans “approved” in writing or stamp. One set of plans so approved
shall be retained by the Building Inspector and the other set shall be returned
to the applicant. The latter set of approved plans shall be kept at the site of
work and shall be open to inspection by the Building Inspector or his or her
authorized representative.

   (B)   The Building Inspector shall keep a permanent and accurate accounting
of all permit fees and other monies collected, the names of all persons on
whose account the money was paid, and the date and amount thereof.

   In case any building or structure is erected, constructed, reconstructed,
repaired, converted or maintained, or any building, structure or land is used
in violation of this subchapter, the city, its Building Inspector or other

institute injunction, mandamus, abatement or other appropriate action to
prevent, enjoin, abate or remove the unlawful erection, construction,
reconstruction, alteration, maintenance or use.

INHABITABLE PROPERTY WHERE METHAMPHETAMINE HAS BEEN MANUFACTURED; OCCUPANCY
§ 151.40 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purpose of this subchapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   DECONTAMINATION STANDARD. The standards set forth in the administrative
regulations relating to the decontamination of property where the unlawful
manufacture of methamphetamine has taken place as promulgated by the Kentucky
Energy and Environment Cabinet and codified at 401 KAR 101:040, as same may be
amended from time to time.
   INHABITABLE PROPERTY. Any building or structure that is intended to be
occupied by people as a residence or place of lodging, whether such residency
or lodging be temporary or permanent, including, without limitation, houses,
duplexes, multi-plexes, apartments, condominiums, townhouses, mobile homes, bed
and breakfast facilities, and hotel and motel rooms.
   PROPERTY OWNER. The person or entity identified as the owner of the property
in question and at the address reflected by the records on file in the office
of the Boyd County Property Valuation Administrator.
   PROPERTY WHERE METHAMPHETAMINE HAS BEEN MANUFACTURED or PROPERTY.
Inhabitable property in which the unlawful manufacture of methamphetamine has
taken place as confirmed by a state or local law enforcement agency and:
      (1)   In the case of a house, the entire house;
      (2)   In the case of a duplex, multi-plex, apartment building, townhouse
building or condominium building, the entirety of the individual residence
wherein methamphetamine was manufactured;
      (3)   In the case of a mobile home, the entire mobile home; or
      (4)   In the case of a bed and breakfast facility or of a hotel or motel,
the individual room wherein methamphetamine was manufactured.
(Prior Code, § 151.40) (Ord. 49-2013, passed 6-6-2013)
§ 151.41 RESIDENCY OR OTHER OCCUPATION PROHIBITED.
   (A)   When property where methamphetamine has been manufactured has been
identified, the city’s codes enforcement personnel shall:
      (1)   Except in the case of an individual room in a bed and breakfast
facility or in a hotel or motel, post on such property in a conspicuous
location a placard bearing the word “Condemned”;
      (2)   Require that the property be vacated; and
      (3)   Serve on the owner of such property or the person responsible for
the property or the management thereof a notice stating:
         (a)   That the property has been condemned and declared unfit for
human occupancy;
         (b)   The reason for such condemnation and declaration;
         (c)   That the property shall remain condemned, unoccupied, and
declared to be unfit for human occupancy until such time as abatement as
hereinafter set forth has taken place; and
         (d)   The steps required to effect abatement as hereinafter set forth.
   (B)   Any property where methamphetamine has been manufactured and condemned
by the Code Enforcement Official shall be immediately vacated as ordered by the
Code Enforcement Official. Any person who shall occupy property so condemned,
and any owner or person responsible for the property or the management thereof
who shall permit the occupation of such condemned property, shall be guilty of
a violation.
(Prior Code, § 151.41) (Ord. 49-2013, passed 6-6-2013) Penalty, see §
151.99
§ 151.42 NOTIFICATION TO OCCUPANTS OF OTHER DWELLING UNITS.
   When the property where methamphetamine has been manufactured consists of an
individual residence (the “contaminated residence”) in a building which
contains other individual residences (the “other residences”), the Code
Enforcement Official shall endeavor to determine whether the HVAC system which
services the building is such that air from the contaminated residence is
circulated into the other residences as well. If it appears that air is so
circulated, the Code Enforcement Official shall attempt to give notification to
the occupants of the other residences of the fact that methamphetamine has been
manufactured in another residence within the building and that they should take
such steps as they may feel to be appropriate to ensure their safety in
determining whether or not to continue the occupation of the residence in
question.
(Prior Code, § 151.42) (Ord. 49-2013, passed 6-6-2013)
§ 151.43 ABATEMENT; REMOVAL OF PLACARD; OCCUPATION.
   (A)   Property where methamphetamine has been manufactured shall remain
condemned, placarded and unoccupied as set forth above until such time as there
has been presented to the city the written certification, from a contractor
certified within the meaning of KRS 224.01.410(4)(a), that the property either:
      (1)   Upon inspection met the decontamination standard for
methamphetamine and/or methamphetamine precursors; or
      (2)   Has undergone decontamination procedures which have resulted in the
property’s meeting the decontamination standard for methamphetamine and/or
methamphetamine precursors.
   (B)   At such time as such written certification has been produced to the
city’s Department of Code Enforcement, the codes official shall remove the
condemnation placard and, provided that the property is otherwise in conformity
with applicable code requirements, the property may then be occupied.
(Prior Code, § 151.43) (Ord. 49-2013, passed 6-6-2013)
§ 151.44 NOTICE OF CONDEMNATION.
   (A)   The notice of condemnation required under the provisions of §
151.41 shall:
      (1)   Be in writing;
      (2)   Include a description of the property where methamphetamine has
been manufactured sufficient for identification;
      (3)   Contain the information set forth in §
151.41 of this section; and
      (4)   Be served upon the property owner.
   (B)   Notice shall be conclusively deemed to have been properly served on
the property owner if a copy thereof is:
      (1)   Delivered personally;
      (2)   Sent by first-class mail; or
      (3)   If the mailed notice is returned showing that it was not delivered,
a copy thereof shall be posted in a conspicuous place in or about the structure
affected by such notice.
   (C)   In the case of a hotel, motel or bed and breakfast facility with
management or clerical staff on the premises and containing property where
methamphetamine has been manufactured, the notice shall further be personally
delivered to one or more of such management or clerical staff on the premises
at such time as the Code Enforcement Official is on premises for such purposes.
(Prior Code, § 151.44) (Ord. 49-2013, passed 6-6-2013)
ELECTRICAL STANDARDS
§ 151.55 GENERAL PROVISIONS.
   (A)   Scope. This subchapter shall be known and may be cited as the
“Electrical Ordinance of the City of Ashland, Kentucky”.
   (B)   Purpose. This subchapter is hereby declared to be remedial and shall
be construed to secure the beneficial interests and purposes of public safety,
health and welfare, through structural strength and stability, and safety of
life and property from fire hazards incidental to installation, alteration,
repair and/or removal of the electrical wiring or equipment.
   (C)   Compliance with national code. All electrical wiring in installation
of electrical apparatus and appliances for furnishing light, heat or power in
the city, from and after March 13, 2014, shall comply in all respects with the
rules and regulations of the National Electric Code of the National Fire
Protection Association as issued, revised and in effect from time to time
hereafter, and with the provisions of this subchapter, the laws of the
Commonwealth of Kentucky and other applicable ordinances of the city, as now
exist and as may be amended.
   (D)   Resistance electric heating. All installations of resistance electric
heating shall comply with the latest recommendations of the American Society of
Heating and Air Conditioning Engineers.
(Prior Code, § 151.55) (Ord. 21-2014, passed 3-13-2014)
§ 151.56 ELECTRICAL INSPECTOR.
   (A)   Position of Electrical Inspector.
      (1)   There is hereby created the position of Electrical Inspector, said
party(ies) to be appointed by the Board of City Commissioners and shall report
to the Director of Planning and Community Development. The position shall be
filled by contract unless the Board determines otherwise. A person(s) chosen to
act as an Electrical Inspector shall be a competent electrician(s) of good
moral character and certified as an electrical inspector for residential and
commercial uses by the Department of Housing, Building and Construction,
Electrical Division, Commonwealth of Kentucky.
      (2)   He or she shall have substantial bona fide experience in
construction of work and shall have such extensive ability as required for the
faithful performance of his or her duties, and shall have a thorough knowledge
of standard materials and methods used in the installation of electrical wiring
devices, appliances and equipment. He or she shall be well versed in approved
methods of electrical construction to assure the safety of life and property,
the laws of the Commonwealth of Kentucky and the ordinances of the city,
relating to electrical work, the rules and regulations issued under the
authority of the Kentucky Revised Statutes and the National Electrical Code. In
the discretion of the Department Director, alternate persons may be named to
conduct electrical inspections, as may be required from time to time. It shall
be unlawful for any Electrical Inspector or any of his or her authorized
assistants, agents or employees, to engage in the business of sales,
installation or maintenance of electric wiring devices, appliances or
equipment, either directly or indirectly, and he or she shall not have any
financial interest in any business or enterprise engaged in such electrical
business in the city at any time while such individual is the Electrical
Inspector for the city.
   (B)   Duties. It shall be the duty of the Electrical Inspector to see that
the provisions of this subchapter are enforced and to enforce within the city
the laws of the Commonwealth relating to the installation of electrical wiring,
devices, appliances and equipment. He or she shall make inspections of all new
electrical installations as set out herein. He or she shall keep records of all
permits issued, inspections and reinspections made and other official work
performed in accordance with the provisions of this subchapter and such records
shall be available for review at the request of the Department Director.
(Prior Code, § 151.56) (Ord. 21-2014, passed 3-13-2014)
§ 151.57 APPROVAL REQUIRED ON NEW INSTALLATION.
   All electrical wiring, apparatus and appliances hereafter installed in the
city shall be inspected by the Electrical Inspector; and it shall be unlawful
to use any new electrical installation in any building before the same has been
inspected and approved by the city’s Electrical Inspector.
(Prior Code, § 151.57) (Ord. 21-2014, passed 3-13-2014) Penalty, see §
151.99
§ 151.58 INSPECTION OF BUILDINGS; DISCONNECTION OF DEFECTIVE ELECTRICAL
EQUIPMENT.
   (A)   The Electrical Inspector shall have the right, during reasonable
hours, to enter any building or premises in the discharge of his or her
official duties, or for the purpose of making inspections, reinspection or
tests of electrical equipment contained therein or its installation. When any
electrical equipment is found by the Electrical Inspector not to be in
accordance with the standards of the National Electrical Code and/or to be
dangerous to persons or property because of its substandard or defective
installation or maintenance, the person, firm or corporation responsible for
this electrical equipment shall be notified in writing of said defects and must
enter upon any changes or repairs required in said notice within ten days and
further, shall pursue said changes and repairs to diligent completion.
   (B)   If, during his or her inspections, the Electrical Inspector shall find
that electrical wiring, appliances, installations or equipment do not meet the
standard of the National Electrical Code and the Electrical Inspector has
reasonable cause to believe that such faulty installation or maintenance
creates a condition of immediate peril and/or danger to persons and/or
property, then he or she shall immediately order the disconnection of such
electrical equipment. No such order of disconnection shall be made by the
Electrical Inspector unless he or she shall serve on the owner or operator and
upon the local power company, written notice of his or her findings and the
violations revealed by his or her inspection requiring the immediate
disconnection. The owner/operator of the property in question shall have the
right to appeal the order of the Electrical Inspector. It shall be unlawful for
any person, form or corporation, to reconnect electrical power to electric
wiring, appliances, equipment or installations while the such appliances,
equipment or installations are under an order of disconnection.
(Prior Code, § 151.58) (Ord. 21-2014, passed 3-13-2014) Penalty, see §
151.99
§ 151.59 NOTICE OF INTENTION TO INSTALL WIRING OR MAKE ALTERATIONS; EXCEPTIONS.
   No electric wiring devices, appliances or equipment shall be installed
within or on, any building structure or premises, nor shall any alterations be
made in existing wiring devices, appliances or equipment without notifying the
Electrical Inspector and obtaining a permit.
(Prior Code, § 151.59) (Ord. 21-2014, passed 3-13-2014) Penalty, see §
151.99
§ 151.60 PERMITS.
   Permits shall be required before commencing construction, alteration or
repair of any electrical wiring within the city pursuant to the Kentucky
Building Code and the Kentucky Residential Code as promulgated in 815 KAR 7:120
and 7:125, respectively, and all other applicable laws of the Commonwealth.
(Prior Code, § 151.60) (Ord. 21-2014, passed 3-13-2014) Penalty, see §
151.99

inspections for the project shall be performed by another duly appointed city
Electrical Inspector.
